Cracks Beneath the Shadow of Nineteen Eighty-Four: The Possibility of Big Brother’s Rule Collapsing
George Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four depicts a totalitarian world—Oceania—where Big Brother’s omnipresence and power grip are as tight as steel, creating a suffocating sense of oppression. The novel ultimately concludes with Winston’s complete surrender to “Big Brotherization,” seemingly foreshadowing the futility of individual resistance. However, if we delve into the internal logic of this meticulously constructed totalitarian regime and imagine its possible evolution under high-pressure rule, we might glimpse a faint glimmer of hope, suggesting that the seemingly indestructible fortress of Big Brother will eventually crumble.
Inherent Corruption of Totalitarian Rule and the Alienation of the “Thought Police” In the world of Nineteen Eighty-Four, the extreme concentration of power, the lack of checks and balances, and the dogma that “Big Brother is Always Right” inevitably breed the tumors of corruption and bureaucracy. If we imagine the story continuing, we can foresee the following developments:
Rent-Seeking and the Illusion of “Good Days”: Party officials who control resource allocation, such as those responsible for “patriotic rations,” will find it difficult to resist the absolute temptation of power. They will use their authority to secure private benefits for themselves and their cronies, secretly funneling scarce resources to their connections, enriching themselves, and enjoying “good days,” while ordinary citizens struggle amidst endless shortages. This rent-seeking spreads like a tumor, fundamentally eroding the body of the Party and shaking the populace’s faith in “Ingsoc.” Bureaucratic Bloat and Inefficiency under “Newspeak”: To maintain the massive surveillance and propaganda machinery, the bureaucracy is bound to swell like an inflated balloon. Various departments, competing for scarce resources and seeking to gain favor, will fall into endless internal friction and shirking of responsibility, leading to low policy execution efficiency and rampant resource waste. While the use of “Newspeak” might mask temporary problems, it cannot prevent the continuous slide in efficiency. Information is distorted as it passes through layers; lower-level officials, in order to please their superiors, may inflate reports of “exceeding production targets” and conceal the spread of “thought crimes,” ultimately causing a severe disconnect between central decision-making and brutal reality. The Arbitrary Actions of the “Thought Police” and the Spread of Fear: The “Thought Police,” unrestrained by any authority, will increasingly abuse their power to meet quotas, gain praise, or simply out of personal grudges. They will arbitrarily arrest, interrogate, and even “vaporize” the innocent who are suspected of committing “thought crimes.” Initially, this fear might deter people, but as the abuses multiply, it will gradually evolve into a pervasive sense of insecurity and social distrust, even turning against the regime itself. The “Thought Police” cease to be a tool for maintaining order; instead, they become the source of chaos and fear. Controlled Shortages Spiral Out of Control and the Outbreak of a Livelihood Crisis The Big Brother regime artificially creates “controlled shortages” to strengthen control over the populace, forcing them to focus their energy on survival rather than thought. However, the aforementioned corruption, inefficiency, and resource misallocation will make this fragile balance unsustainable, eventually evolving into an uncontrollable, all-consuming livelihood crisis:
The Food Crisis under “Doublethink”: Due to corruption, mismanagement, and false propaganda regarding agricultural production, food output will continuously decline. The “rationing” system becomes nominal; allocated supplies are either devoured by officials or simply non-existent. The lower classes will remain perpetually on the brink of starvation, with survival becoming their sole preoccupation. “Doublethink” cannot fill stomachs; loyalty to the Party becomes pale and powerless in the face of hunger. Total Scarcity of Daily Necessities: Beyond food, other daily necessities, such as shoddy “uniform clothing” and inadequate heating fuel, will also suffer severe shortages due to similar corruption and inefficiency, leaving the populace in dire straits. The already bleak world will become even more desperate due to extreme material scarcity. The Rise of the Black Market and the Erosion of Big Brother’s Authority: Under immense pressure to survive, people will take risks and participate in black market transactions to acquire essential supplies. There, they might exchange information about the truth of the resource shortages, or meet others who are equally dissatisfied with the status quo. The existence of the black market, to a certain extent, weakens the Party’s control over resources and information, planting a dangerous seed for future resistance and becoming a secret channel for dismantling Big Brother’s authority. Social Upheaval Triggered by Hunger and the Spread of “Thought Crimes” When basic sustenance becomes a distant dream, the propaganda of “Newspeak” and ideological indoctrination become hollow and ridiculous. “When a man is hungry for several days, all he thinks about is: having a full meal.” The instinct for survival will override everything else, and social order will begin to collapse. The initial feeling of hunger will gradually transform into a profound questioning of Big Brother’s rule:
Desperate Foraging and the Hypocrisy of “Two Minutes Hate”: Hungry people will begin to spontaneously and desperately search for food. They may raid empty granaries, loot the few remaining shops, or even direct their anger toward the Party and state organs that control the remaining resources. Isolated conflicts will gradually increase; the populace is no longer afraid of the “Thought Police”; their only fear is hunger. The once intense “Two Minutes Hate” appears hypocritical and ridiculous in the face of empty stomachs. The Collapse of Social Order and the Failure of the “Telescreen”: Large-scale foraging efforts will lead to social chaos. Theft and robbery will increase sharply, and the government’s control capacity will significantly decline. The “Telescreen” continues to broadcast deafening propaganda, but it can no longer mask the social disorder and the populace’s despair. The Emergence of Secret Gatherings and the Collapse of the Big Brother Image: Driven by hunger, people may secretly gather in the darkness to discuss countermeasures, yearning to overthrow the regime responsible for all this. The truth about government corruption and resource shortages will quietly circulate among the masses, spreading like wildfire, awakening the people’s consciousness of resistance. Big Brother’s omnipresent face gradually loses its former deterrent power, replaced by the anger and disappointment in the hearts of the people. The Natural Vulnerability of Power Transition in Totalitarian Rule Big Brother’s Limited Lifespan: Even in the novel, Big Brother is not a god; he will eventually age and die. This is an unavoidable biological fact, and any rule built upon personal worship must face this reality. The Danger Period of Power Transition: Regardless of how power is transferred, the transition period from one “Big Brother” to the next will inevitably involve a power vacuum and uncertainty. This is a high-risk phase for any regime, especially a totalitarian one, whose legitimacy is largely built upon the personal worship of the supreme leader. Lack of Clear Succession Mechanism: Nineteen Eighty-Four does not mention any system or arrangement regarding Big Brother’s successor. This may be because: Big Brother is shaped as an eternal symbol: Emphasizing his irreplaceable nature to solidify his mythical status. Potential internal power struggles within the Party: The unclear succession mechanism may actually leave room for internal elites to fight for supreme power after Big Brother’s death. Limitations of Hereditary Succession: Even if an attempt is made to continue Big Brother’s rule through father-son succession, it faces practical problems such as lack of offspring, insufficient capability of the offspring, or disloyalty of the offspring. Risks Big Brother’s Rule May Face During Power Transition: Legitimacy Crisis: Once the real Big Brother dies, the successor (whoever they may be) will struggle to fully inherit the predecessor’s divine aura and absolute authority. The populace may question: Is this person truly “Big Brother”? This doubt will shake the foundation of the rule, providing opportunities for potential challengers.
Outbreak of Internal Party Power Struggles: If Big Brother dies without a clear heir, or if the designated successor lacks sufficient prestige, different factions within the Party are likely to engage in fierce struggles for supreme power. This struggle may become public, leading to party division and internal friction, greatly weakening its ruling power. It may even lead to different factions proclaiming different “Big Brothers,” triggering civil war.
Shaking of Public Faith: Once the myth of “Big Brother” is broken, the ideological system long instilled in the populace may develop cracks. They may begin to question the dogma that “Big Brother is Always Right,” and even reflect on their blind worship of the Party in the past. This provides an ideological basis for potential resistance.
Increased Difficulty in Information Control: During the sensitive period of power transition, different Party factions may attempt to seize control of the propaganda machine to strike at their rivals and consolidate their own position. This could lead to chaos in information channels, making it difficult to maintain absolute monopoly over information, and may allow news about Big Brother’s true condition to leak out, further shaking public trust.
Intervention of External Forces: If Oceania remains in a state of war, Big Brother’s death and the chaos of the power transition may be seen as an opportunity by Eurasia or Eastasia, triggering new conflicts or intensifying subversive efforts.
The Growth of Revolutionary Forces and the End of the Big Brother Myth The spontaneous resistance initially driven by hunger may gradually develop into an organized revolutionary force, and the suppressed reason and humanity will gradually return:
Joining of Former Party Members and the Bankruptcy of “Doublethink”: Some former Party members, dissatisfied with the Party for various reasons or even purged, may step forward to lead the revolution. They understand the Party’s operational patterns and weaknesses better, enabling them to provide more effective strategies and organization. The “Doublethink” they once believed in also completely collapses, and they begin to examine this diseased society with clear minds. Expansion of the Popular Base and Shaking of the Military: As hunger spreads, more and more people join the ranks of the resistance, and the revolutionary force grows. Long-term hunger and despair about the future may also affect military morale; some soldiers may sympathize with the suffering populace and even choose to defect, joining the ranks to overthrow Big Brother. Internal Party Power Struggles and the Fall of Big Brother: When the regime faces a severe crisis, different Party factions may publicly split to fight for power, further weakening the Party’s rule. Some ambitious figures may see the opportunity to overthrow Big Brother and replace him, no longer viewing “Big Brother” as an untouchable, sacred entity. The Final Collapse and the Dawn of Freedom: Under the combined influence of multiple factors, a large-scale popular uprising may erupt, challenging the Party’s center of power. Big Brother, as the symbol of totalitarian rule, once his authority is broken, the entire regime’s legitimacy vanishes. Oceania may finally collapse like a giant beast consumed by internal decay, ushering in a new era full of uncertainty but also hope. People begin to relearn the words erased by “Newspeak” and start reclaiming the suppressed true emotions. Conclusion Although Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four presents a seemingly indestructible totalitarian regime, a deep analysis of its internal mechanisms reveals its fatal weaknesses. The corruption of officials, the alienation of the “Thought Police,” the inefficiency of the bureaucracy, and the resulting livelihood crisis—these act like termites gnawing at the dam, eroding the foundation of this vast empire. When survival becomes the primary concern, the meticulously constructed ideological barrier will crumble, and the hungry populace will unleash unimaginable forces of resistance. Of course, the path to freedom will inevitably be fraught with thorns, but history has proven countless times that any rule that defies human nature will eventually meet its demise. Our speculation on a sequel to Nineteen Eighty-Four may be a rational extrapolation of this historical law, carrying the hope that the brilliance of humanity will ultimately triumph over darkness.
summary:
Cracks Beneath the Shadow of Nineteen Eighty-Four: The Possibility of Big Brother’s Rule Collapsing

The novel ultimately concludes with Winston’s complete surrender to “Big Brotherization,” seemingly foreshadowing the futility of individual resistance. However, if we delve into the internal logic of this meticulously constructed totalitarian regime and imagine its possible evolution under high-pressure rule, we might glimpse a faint glimmer of hope, suggesting that the seemingly indestructible fortress of Big Brother will eventually crumble.

The Brainwashing of Children: A Cornerstone of the Party’s Strategy The brainwashing of children to betray their parents is a cornerstone of the Party’s strategy, and it yields several significant benefits for Big Brother and the Party’s control:
Here’s a breakdown of the benefits:
1. Elimination of Dissent and Thoughtcrime: Internal Spies and Early Detection: Children, thoroughly indoctrinated from a young age, become the perfect internal spies within the family unit. They are highly attuned to any deviation from Party orthodoxy, any flicker of independent thought, or any sign of “thoughtcrime” in their parents. This allows the Party to detect and crush dissent at its earliest stages, before it can spread or organize.
Preemptive Suppression: The fear of being denounced by one’s own children creates a climate of constant self-censorship. Parents become hyper-vigilant about their words, actions, and even thoughts around their children, stifling any potential rebellious ideas before they can even be voiced.
Undermining Family Loyalty: The family unit, traditionally a source of love, loyalty, and independent values, is deliberately targeted. By turning children against their parents, the Party destroys this vital social structure and ensures that the primary loyalty of individuals is directed solely towards Big Brother.
2. Instilling Fear and Absolute Control: Ubiquitous Surveillance: The knowledge that even your own children could be your betrayers reinforces the Party’s message of constant surveillance. It creates a sense that nowhere is truly safe, and no one can be trusted. This pervasive fear paralyzes individuals and makes them more compliant.
Psychological Warfare: The betrayal by one’s own offspring is a deeply traumatic experience. It shatters the fundamental bonds of love and trust. This psychological devastation weakens individuals and makes them more susceptible to the Party’s manipulation.
Demonstration of Power: The Party’s ability to manipulate children to such an extent showcases its absolute power. It demonstrates that the Party can control even the most primal instincts and loyalties, reinforcing its image as an unchallengeable force.
3. Perpetuation of the Party’s Ideology: Early Indoctrination and Inculcation: Brainwashing children from a young age is incredibly effective. Their minds are more malleable, and they absorb the Party’s doctrines without question. This ensures that the next generation will be even more deeply ingrained with the Party’s ideology than the current one.
Active Participation in Enforcement: By encouraging children to denounce their parents, the Party makes them active participants in the enforcement of its will. This not only reinforces their own indoctrination but also makes them feel invested in the system, as they have directly contributed to upholding it.
Normalization of Betrayal: Making betrayal a pathway to merit and reward normalizes this behavior. It becomes a part of the social fabric, further eroding trust and empathy within society.
4. Weakening Individual Identity and Independence: Erosion of Personal Relationships: When the most fundamental relationships are poisoned by fear and suspicion, individuals become isolated and dependent on the Party for social connection and belonging.
Suppression of Empathy and Compassion: The act of betraying one’s parents requires a suppression of natural empathy and compassion. This aligns with the Party’s goal of eliminating any emotions or sentiments that could challenge its authority.
In essence, Big Brother benefits from children betraying their parents by: Creating a society where independent thought is actively policed from within. Instilling a deep and pervasive fear that ensures obedience. Destroying traditional bonds of loyalty and replacing them with devotion to the Party. Guaranteeing the long-term survival and perpetuation of its ideology. It’s a deeply disturbing tactic, but it highlights the Party’s ruthless and comprehensive approach to maintaining absolute power. The scene with the Parsons children denouncing their father is a powerful illustration of this chillingly effective method of control.

Does the Ministry of Truth Personally Insult Big Brother? This is a very good question, touching upon the core operational principle of the “Two Minutes Hate” mechanism in 1984. On the surface, the broadcast of Emmanuel Goldstein cursing Big Brother seems to weaken Big Brother’s sacred status, but in reality, this is one of the key strategies the Ministry of Truth uses to maintain its rule.
Here are several explanations for why the Ministry of Truth does this, and how this action actually helps solidify the image of Big Brother:
1. Creating External Enemies, Shifting Internal Conflicts:
Setting a Target: Goldstein is the “public enemy” meticulously crafted by the Party, serving as the target onto which all social problems and dissatisfaction are projected. By showcasing his “ugly” words, the Party can direct the populace’s anger and frustration toward a fictional enemy, rather than toward the Party itself. Achieving Unity: A common enemy is one of the most effective ways to unite a group. The “Two Minutes Hate” forces the populace to collectively vent their hatred for Goldstein, and this collective emotional release creates a false sense of unity, making people feel that they are standing with Big Brother against evil forces. 2. Strengthening Loyalty to the Party:
Striking Contrast: Goldstein’s “evil” forms a stark contrast with Big Brother’s “greatness.” By displaying Goldstein’s “lies” and “rebelliousness,” Big Brother’s image is highlighted as being more brilliant, heroic, and worthy of devotion. Emotional Manipulation: The “Two Minutes Hate” is a high-intensity form of emotional manipulation. Negative emotions such as anger, fear, and hatred are deliberately stimulated, and in this heightened emotional state, people’s critical thinking is weakened, making them more receptive to the Party’s propaganda and directives. Proving the Party’s Correctness: Goldstein’s existence is used to prove that all the Party’s policies and actions are rational, because he represents “evil,” and the Party is actively fighting him. 3. Suppressing Dissent, Reinforcing Fear:
Showing the “Consequences” of Dissent: Goldstein’s fate is implied to be tragic, serving as a warning to any potential dissenter. Displaying his “rebellion” is essentially reminding people that any act opposing the Party will be met with scorn and punishment, just like Goldstein. Controlling the Flow of Information: The Ministry of Truth completely controls the dissemination of information. The image of Goldstein they present is carefully filtered and distorted, not to allow people to truly understand his thoughts, but to incite hatred. 4. Ritualistic Control:
The Daily Ritual: The “Two Minutes Hate” has become a daily ritual, much like morning calisthenics, integrated into people’s lives. This ritualistic behavior reinforces the Party’s authority and makes people accustomed to accepting the Party’s arrangements. Collective Obedience: Participating in the “Two Minutes Hate” is a public expression of obedience and loyalty to the Party. Refusing to participate or showing insufficient “enthusiasm” will be viewed as suspicious, potentially even incurring punishment. In summary, the broadcast of Goldstein cursing Big Brother, while seemingly risky on the surface, is a meticulously designed strategy by the Ministry of Truth, aimed at:
Creating enemies and shifting conflicts. Strengthening loyalty and consolidating rule. Suppressing dissent and manufacturing fear. Ritualistic control and taming the populace. This reflects a profound insight in 1984 into how an authoritarian regime utilizes psychological tactics and propaganda to maintain control. By manipulating the emotions and cognition of the populace, the Party can make them believe a false narrative and direct their hatred toward predetermined targets, thereby solidifying its own power.
Of course, all of this occurs in a fictional world. Our discussion today is purely based on the understanding and analysis of this novel.
Upgraded Version: Hate Week Purpose and Importance of Hate Week:
Intensifying Hate, Shifting Conflicts: Hate Week is an upgrade to the “Two Minutes Hate,” a week-long intensive propaganda campaign designed to push the populace’s hatred to a fever pitch and focus this hatred on the currently designated enemy (whether it be Eurasia or Eastasia, the shifting of the enemy in the novel is itself a manifestation of the Party controlling reality). This effectively diverts public dissatisfaction from domestic issues, such as shortages of supplies or hardship in daily life. Consolidating Loyalty, Manufacturing Frenzy: Through massive propaganda, speeches, parades, and singing, Hate Week creates an atmosphere of collective frenzy, forcing everyone to publicly express their loyalty to the Party and their hatred for the enemy. Failure to participate or showing insufficient enthusiasm will be viewed as heresy. Demonstrating Party Authority and Mobilization Capacity: Successfully holding Hate Week requires the Party’s vast propaganda machine and organizational capability. Saving electricity in advance to ensure sufficient energy supply during Hate Week is a way for the Party to demonstrate its powerful control and resource allocation ability. This also silently reminds the populace that everything is under the Party’s control. Deepening the Demonization of the “Enemy”: Hate Week spares no effort in depicting the enemy as evil and brutal, thereby rationalizing the rule of Big Brother and the Party, and preparing public opinion for possible war. Why Save Electricity in Advance?
Preparation for Large-Scale Propaganda Activities: During Hate Week, there will be numerous propaganda activities requiring electrical support, such as: Mass Gatherings and Speeches: Requiring lighting and amplification equipment. Television and Film Broadcasts: Displaying hate propaganda content on screens scattered everywhere. Printing and Broadcasting: Although electricity may not directly power the printing presses, related logistics and information transmission may require it. Surveillance and Security: To maintain order, additional monitoring and security measures may be needed, which also require electricity. Reflecting Planned Economy and Unified Allocation: Saving electricity in advance and concentrating it for Hate Week demonstrates the Party’s unified planning and allocation of resources. This is a symbolic act, showing that the Party can sacrifice the populace’s daily convenience for important political objectives. Creating an Atmosphere of “Sacrifice for a Greater Goal”: It makes the populace realize that Hate Week is an extremely important political task, requiring everyone’s collective effort, even if it means sacrificing some of the daily electricity supply. This atmosphere helps elevate the status and influence of Hate Week. Further Controlling People’s Lives: Saving electricity in advance is also a manifestation of the Party further controlling the populace’s daily life. Even seemingly minor electricity usage is under the Party’s planning and control. Summary:
The detail of saving electricity in advance for Hate Week, while seemingly simple energy allocation, actually reflects the operational logic of the totalitarian regime in 1984:
Everything serves the Party’s rule. Power is maintained through propaganda and emotional control. Refined control over social resources. Shifting internal conflicts by creating external enemies. This detail further emphasizes that in the world of 1984, individual life is completely dominated by political goals, and even daily electricity usage has become a tool of political struggle.

Since the Cognitive Revolution, humanity has lived in a dual reality. On one hand, we have the objective reality that truly exists, such as rivers, trees, and lions; on the other hand, we have the imagined reality, such as God, the nation, and the corporation.
One of the few unshakable truths throughout history is that initial luxuries often eventually become necessities, bringing with them new obligations. Once we become accustomed to a certain luxury, we begin to believe it is natural or self-evident. This leads to a dependency. Eventually, life cannot proceed without that luxury.
“A bayonet certainly can do many things, but it is not very comfortable to sit on it.”

What maintains military order? It is clearly not feasible to maintain military organization solely through threats. At the very least, certain officers and certain soldiers must genuinely believe in certain things, whether it is faith in God, honor, the homeland, masculinity, or simply believing in money.
Whether it is Christianity, democracy, or capitalism, they are all orders built by imagination. But how do we make people believe in these orders?
First, the external assertion must absolutely insist that they are certain and absolutely not fictional. We must always emphasize that this order, which maintains social stability, is an objective fact created by a great God or by natural law.
Second, the same principles must be thoroughly implemented in education. From the moment a person is born, they must be constantly reminded that this order, built by imagination, must be integrated into everything—whether it is fairy tales, plays, paintings, songs, rituals, political propaganda, architecture, recipes, or fashion.
The order built by imagination is deeply integrated with the real world. Although these orders built by imagination only exist in our minds, they can be tightly integrated and inseparable from the real world. For example, most Westerners today believe in individualism, believing that every person is an independent entity with independent value, unaffected by the opinions of others.
The order built by imagination shapes our desires. For most people, it is difficult to accept that their life order is merely a fictional imagination, but the fact is that we are immersed in this imagination from birth, and even our desires are deeply influenced by it. Consequently, personal desire becomes the strongest guardian of the fictional order.
The desires most valued by modern Westerners are built…
Even the desires that people think are deeply hidden within themselves are usually influenced by the order built by imagination. For example, many people long to vacation abroad. However, there is no natural or obvious reason for this. For instance, a chimpanzee leader would not want to use power to take a vacation in the territory of a neighboring chimpanzee. Similarly, the Pharaohs of ancient Egypt would take all their wealth to build pyramids and mummify their bodies, rather than wanting to go to Babylon for a spree or ski in Phoenicia.
We are constantly hearing romantic myths telling us, “That experience opened my eyes, and from then on, my entire life was different.”
The order built by imagination exists in the connection of human thoughts. Even if we assume that through some supernatural power, my desires break free from this order built by imagination, I am still only one person. To change this order, I must convince millions of strangers to cooperate with me. The reason is: the order built by imagination is not a personal subjective imagination, but exists within the shared imagination of millions of people—this is what is called intersubjectivity.

The existence of “objective” things is not affected by human consciousness and belief.
The existence of “subjective” things relies on the consciousness and belief of a single individual. If this person changes their belief, this subjective thing ceases to exist, or changes along with it. For example, many children imagine they have a friend only they can see and hear. This imagined friend exists only in the child’s subjective consciousness; when the child grows up and stops believing, this friend vanishes from the world.
The existence of “intersubjectivity” relies on the network of connections between many individual subjective consciousnesses. Even if one person changes their mind, or even passes away, the impact on this phenomenon is not great. But if the majority of people in this network die, or change their minds, this intersubjectivity will disappear, or change.
Let us take the example of the Porsche car again. This company is not a friend imagined solely by the Porsche CEO; it exists in the shared imagination of millions of people.
Similarly, whether it is the US dollar, human rights, or America, they exist in the shared imagination of billions of people, and any single individual is powerless to shake these concepts. Even if I personally resolve to stop believing in the dollar, human rights, and America, it cannot cause any change. Precisely because these orders built by imagination possess intersubjectivity, if we want to change them, we must simultaneously change the thoughts of billions of people—this is by no means easy. To achieve such large-scale change, complex organizations must assist behind the scenes, perhaps political parties, perhaps ideological movements, or perhaps a certain religious sect. However, to establish such a complex organization, we must convince many strangers to cooperate, and this, in turn, requires them to believe in other shared fictional stories.
Even the Declaration of Independence of 1776, although proclaiming “all men are created equal” with a thunderous roar, actually divides people into upper and lower classes. The Declaration distinguishes between men and women, benefiting men, but stripping women of the same rights. The Declaration also distinguishes between white, Black, and Indigenous people, allowing white people to enjoy liberal democracy, but considering Black and Indigenous people to be relatively inferior humans who should not enjoy equal rights. Many slave owners signed the Declaration at the time; they did not free their slaves after signing, but they did not feel hypocritical at all. In their view, what “human” rights did a Black person have?
The iron law of history tells us that every order built by imagination absolutely refuses to admit that it originated from imagination and fiction, but instead boasts that it is the natural, inevitable result.
However, as far as we currently know, these class distinctions are all products of human imagination. Whether one is a Brahmin or a Shudra, they were not created from different organs of some original being.
But the facts have proven that most rich people are rich simply because they were born into wealthy families, and most poor people remain poor simply because they were born into poor families.
The facts have proven that most rich people are rich simply because they were born into wealthy families, and most poor people remain poor simply because they were born into poor families.
Class has its important function. Once there are classes, strangers do not have to waste time and energy truly understanding each other; they also know how to treat each other.
Even if people from different classes develop completely identical abilities, because they face different rules of the game, the final results may be vastly different. For example, suppose in India under British rule, there are four people with completely identical business acumen, but the four people are a Dalit, a Brahmin, a Catholic Irishman, and a Protestant Englishman. Their probability of becoming wealthy will still be significantly different.
But no one admits that they treat certain races or origins as slaves merely for economic gain.
Saying: “A good man should not be a soldier; good iron should not be hammered into a nail.”
Money is a system of mutual trust. Whether it is a shell or a US dollar, its value exists only in our shared imagination. Merely its chemical structure, color, or shape cannot bring that value. In other words, money is not a material reality, but merely a psychological imagination.
Money is the most universal and effective system of mutual trust in history.
If a wealthy farmer sells his house and land and exchanges them for a bag of shells, and then carries this bag of shells to a distant province, it is because he believes that upon arrival, others will be willing to exchange rice, houses, and land for these shells. Therefore, it can be said that money is a system of mutual trust, and it is not just any system: money is the most universal and effective system of mutual trust in history.
Even among Christians and Muslims, who are religiously incompatible, they can achieve the same faith in the monetary system. The reason is that the focus of religious faith is “self-belief,” but the focus of monetary faith is “other-belief.”
The price of money. Second, universal belief: With money as the medium, any two people can cooperate to carry out various plans.
Money also has a darker side. Although money can establish common trust among strangers, what people trust is not humanity, community, or certain sacred values, but money itself, and the system behind it that lacks humanity. We do not trust strangers, but we also do not trust our neighbors; we simply trust the money they hold. Without money, there is no trust. When money permeates and breaks down the dam formed by society, religion, and the state, the world becomes a vast and ruthless market.

Making “them” into “us.” In many cases where small cultures merge into larger cultures, the influence of the empire is paramount. The transmission of ideas, population, goods, and technology within the empire is faster and more convenient than in regions governed by different powers. Moreover, it is often the empire itself that deliberately accelerates the spread of various ideas, institutions, customs, and norms. One reason is that it is easier to govern.
The importance of the second reason cannot be underestimated: by actively spreading common culture, the empire strengthens its legitimacy to rule.
Although imperial civilization may conquer and fuse the cultures of various ethnic groups, for the vast majority of members of the empire, the mixed results still feel unfamiliar. The process of assimilation often carries pain and trauma.

These gods specialize in certain areas, rather than being all-encompassing, so there are gods of the elephant head, gods of wealth, and gods of wisdom, etc., but they all still have their own selfish interests and biases. The past problem was not whether the concept of credit existed or whether people knew how to use it, but because people at the time did not believe that “tomorrow will be better,” so they were unwilling to extend credit. Business looked like a zero-sum game: after opening a bakery, you might indeed make a profit, but it is certainly because you took the profit from the neighboring bakery. If Beijing flourishes, it must be taking resources from Shanghai. If the King of England has overflowing wealth, it must be at the expense of the King of France’s pocket. The whole world is like a big pie, cut in different ways, but ultimately, it is only one pie, and it cannot become bigger.

Unless you believe that the baker (or king) lending you money will seize a larger slice from the competitor, isn’t the risk of borrowing from him too great? Whether it is an entrepreneur wanting to start a new company, or a medieval person wanting to read scriptures, participate in holy wars, or build a new temple, the meaning they derive from it is merely an illusion and a fantasy.
summary:
Since the Cognitive Revolution, humanity has lived in a dual reality. On one hand, we have the objective reality that truly exists, such as rivers, trees, and lions; on the other hand, we have the imagined reality, such as God, the nation, and the corporation.

One of the few unshakable truths throughout history is that initial luxuries often eventually become necessities, bringing with them new obligations. Once we become accustomed to a certain luxury, we begin to believe it is natural or self-evident. This leads to a dependency. Eventually, life cannot proceed without that luxury.
title: Grand History of Humanity
