When discussing economics, Producer Surplus is an important concept. It refers to the difference between the actual income received by a producer or supplier when selling goods in the market at a certain price, and the minimum income they expected when willing to sell those goods at that price.
Simply put, Producer Surplus is the net gain of the producer in a transaction. Its calculation involves two key factors:
Producer’s Supply Price: This refers to the price at which the producer is willing to sell the goods or services. Typically, the producer’s supply price is related to their marginal cost (the extra cost of producing one unit of goods), because they hope to at least cover the production cost.
Market Price: This refers to the price the buyer is willing to pay, which is the market price of the goods or services.
The calculation formula for Producer Surplus is as follows:
Producer Surplus = Producer’s Supply Price - Market Price
Producer Surplus represents the net gain obtained by the producer when selling goods at a lower supply price. Producer Surplus occurs when the market price is higher than the producer’s supply price, because the producer sells the goods at a lower price but receives a higher actual income. If the market price is lower than the producer’s supply price, the Producer Surplus will be negative, meaning the producer may incur a loss in the transaction.
Producer Surplus is very important for understanding market operation and the supply-demand relationship. In a free market, the balance of supply and demand determines the market price, and Producer Surplus helps us understand the producer’s profitability at different price levels. When the market is in equilibrium, Producer Surplus is maximized, meaning the producer achieves maximum profit.
Okay, Consumer Surplus is an economic term that refers to the economic benefit or value obtained by consumers when purchasing goods or services. Its calculation method is:
Consumer Surplus = Consumer’s Reservation Price (Expected Price) - Actual Paid Price
For a simple example, assume the reservation price for an item is 100 Yuan for the consumer. If the actual market price is 80 Yuan, then the Consumer Surplus obtained by that consumer when purchasing the item is 100 - 80 = 20 Yuan.
Consumer Surplus reflects the net gain obtained by the consumer after purchasing goods or services. The larger the Consumer Surplus, the higher the economic utility obtained by the consumer. Increasing Consumer Surplus can usually raise total social welfare. The government employs many measures to increase Consumer Surplus, such as subsidies, tax incentives, etc.
summary:
When discussing economics, Producer Surplus is an important concept. It refers to the difference between the actual income received by a producer or supplier when selling goods in the market at a certain price, and the minimum income they expected when willing to sell those goods at that price.

Simply put, Producer Surplus is the net gain of the producer in a transaction. Its calculation involves two key factors:

Producer’s Supply Price: This refers to the price at which the producer is willing to sell the goods or services. Typically, the producer’s supply price is related to their marginal cost (the extra cost of producing one unit of goods), because they hope to at least cover the production cost.
title: Producer Surplus and Consumer Surplus

In a free competitive market, when the wage level of a certain profession or industry is higher than the value deserved by the labor output or skills for that job, it attracts more people to study that profession and enter that market. As the supply increases, the number of workers in the market grows, which subsequently causes the wage level to decrease, eventually approaching the value deserved by the labor output.
This phenomenon is known in economics as the “Marginal Productivity Theory.” It posits that there is a relationship between the wage level and the marginal output of labor (which is the increase in output generated by adding one unit of labor). When a certain profession’s wage is higher than its marginal output, it attracts more people to join, thereby increasing the labor supply, which in turn lowers the wage level until the marginal output and the wage level reach equilibrium.
This phenomenon is common across many professions and industries. When supply and demand in the market tend towards equilibrium, the wage level usually tends towards the value of the marginal output—this is the situation you mentioned where profit approaches zero. In the long run, the market forms a relatively stable equilibrium state, and the wage level adjusts to match the skills, labor output, and market demand.
This also explains why continuous learning and skill improvement are extremely important for individuals to achieve success and obtain better compensation in the workplace. By constantly improving one’s skills and knowledge, an individual can maintain competitiveness in a fierce market and achieve better economic returns.
If you wish to earn extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself in the labor market, you can consider the following strategies:
Differentiation and Specialization: Find the field or specific skill you excel in, and continuously refine it to become an expert. Through differentiation and specialization, you can provide higher quality and more specialized services, thereby creating higher market value for yourself.
Creating Unique Value: Identify the pain points or needs in the market and provide unique solutions. Understand the customer’s true needs and offer services that exceed their expectations. This can win you more customers and positive word-of-mouth, leading to extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself.
Building a Personal Brand: Establish your visibility and authority in the industry through effective branding and personal promotion. A reputable and credible personal brand can bring you more business opportunities and chances, potentially leading to higher returns.
Mastering Composite Skills: Learning and mastering skills across multiple fields allows you to become a versatile individual. Possessing multiple skills increases your flexibility and adaptability, better meeting market demands, which brings you more opportunities and potential profits.
Innovation and Leadership: Continuously innovating and leading teams to achieve goals can bring you more business opportunities and project collaborations, thereby creating extra profit for you.
It is important to emphasize that pursuing extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself is not easy; it requires a significant investment of time, effort, and resources. Furthermore, success is not achieved overnight; it requires continuous effort and ongoing learning and growth. The key is to find the development path and strategy that suits you and continuously optimize and adjust it through practice. In a fiercely competitive market, only by continuously enhancing your value can you gain more opportunities and profits in the workplace.

As the supply increases, the number of workers in the market grows, which subsequently causes the wage level to decrease, eventually approaching the value deserved by the labor output.
title: What should I do if I want to earn profit beyond the value of the labor itself?

In English, the Third Person Singular refers to the form used for a single third-person subject. In English verbs, the verb form usually changes depending on the person and number of the subject. Specifically, the third person singular refers to situations where the subject is “he,” “she,” “it,” or a single noun. In the present tense, the verb usually takes an “-s” ending when it is in the third person singular.
For example, consider the following sentences:
He plays football.（他踢足球。） She sings beautifully.（她唱得很美。） It runs fast.（它跑得快。） In these examples, “plays,” “sings,” and “runs” are all verbs, and they all have the “-s” ending to match the third person singular subject (“he,” “she,” and “it”).
Please note that the third person singular only applies to the Simple Present Tense. In other tenses, such as the Simple Past Tense, Present Continuous Tense, Simple Future Tense, etc., the verb form will be different.
When discussing English verb tenses, here are some examples of the third person singular across different tenses:
Present Continuous Tense: He is playing football.（他正在踢足球。） She is singing a song.（她正在唱歌。） Present Perfect Tense: He has finished his homework.（他已经完成了作业。） She has gone to the store.（她已经去商店了。） Simple Past Tense: He played basketball yesterday.（他昨天打篮球了。） She danced at the party.（她在聚会上跳舞了。） Past Continuous Tense: He was studying all night.（他整晚都在学习。） She was cooking dinner when the phone rang.（电话响时，她正在做晚饭。） Past Perfect Tense: He had already left when I arrived.（当我到达时，他已经离开了。） She had finished her book before the movie started.（电影开始前，她已经读完了书。） Simple Future Tense: He will play soccer tomorrow.（他明天会踢足球。） She will visit her grandparents next week.（她下周会去看望她的祖父母。） The examples above cover some common English verb tenses and third person singular forms. Different tenses can express different actions or times of events based on the various forms of the main verb and auxiliary verbs.
summary: In English, the Third Person Singular refers to the form used for a single third-person subject. In English verbs, the verb form usually changes depending on the person and number of the subject. Specifically, the third person singular refers to situations where the subject is “he,” “she,” “it,” or a single noun. In the present tense, the verb usually takes an “-s” ending when it is in the third person singular.
title: Simple tenses in English

content: Personally, I think the best way to achieve happiness is to transform life from a multiplayer online game into a single-player game. Online games like PUBG (Chicken Dinner) or Honor of Kings (King’s Land/Arena of Valor) require you to be better than others, have superior gear, and even compare skins. There are always stronger players among the strong, so disappointment is a highly probable event. But what if we change life into a single-player game? For example, Zelda—all you need to do is compare yourself to yourself. Every step is filled with a sense of happiness. Projecting this onto reality means having a better physique than others, a bigger house than others, and a fancier car than others. Constantly thinking about being superior to others, about having to surpass them, makes happiness difficult to achieve. In my opinion, the correct method is: buying a house so you don’t have to move around all the time, happy. Buying a car so you don’t have to squeeze onto the subway, happy. Buying a dishwasher so you don’t have to wash dishes, happy…

content:
Hello everyone, and welcome to the final episode of Deeply Loving Wealth (or Deeply Loving Finance). I’m JS Jing Shu. As for what the future blog or other content will be, I’ll save that for the next episode—that is, the first episode of the new podcast. Since this is the last one, I’m just going to go a little crazy. I’m giving up on being Lin Blogger’s face, or whatever. I’m just done with it.
I want to say something that I’ve always wanted to say: Scholar Cat is toxic. So today, I don’t want to play around with being non-judgmental or making benevolent assumptions about these mind-body-spirit contexts. Because if I hold that idea, of course, it’s not wrong, but my words just won’t make sense, and this sentence will never be fully articulated.
So, today is a very subjective, very emotional episode. This is my background. If you want to say that what he talks about definitely has good aspects, then I agree, of course, but if I keep going back and forth like this, I just can’t produce this episode today. So, just think of it as me going crazy, or maybe even chasing traffic, or maybe you just want to eat some gossip, listen to some chatter—that’s fine. In this episode, I’ll talk about some phenomena I’ve observed in Scholar Cat’s community. But more importantly, I hope you listen to this episode with the following questions in mind. First, what constitutes a toxic thought? How do we define which idea is toxic and which is relatively healthy? Second, why are cults or organizations with extreme and bold ideas so attractive? Third, why does the community easily develop a pathological attachment? And how do we prevent it? Fourth, what are the historical, social, and economic contexts of the mind-body-spirit teachings we are currently exposed to? Have you ever thought about this? And fifth, how do we engage in independent thinking? Since this episode primarily aims to encourage independent thinking, you shouldn’t believe everything I say; you must make your own judgment.
I even feel that if you, hey, truly want to think independently, you’re curious, and you go, but you still spend 999 [currency unit] to join Scholar Mom’s community, or you spend the current 9999, or whatever to buy her course, it doesn’t matter. It means you are truly making a judgment based on your own personal experience. If you have money, you can do that. Right, let me give you another background detail. I also thought that since I am discussing a larger topic today—the entire mind-body-spirit industry—we will talk about the chain of capitalism and consumerism later. Do I need to single out Scholar Cat? And is it better to just talk about the industry to appear more rational, objective, and neutral? But I thought about it, if I just talk about it that way, first, it will be rather dry. Second, my thoughts on this industry are indeed derived from my experience in Scholar Cat’s community. And there are many things that I actually want to express, but due to friendship, or because I want to be a spiritual blogger, I haven’t expressed them.
So I also guess that many of his friends in the community have similar thoughts. So I dare to express some of my very subjective ideas, hoping that through this method, I can make the topic I want to discuss today more concrete—it’s a process of non-self-censorship. Okay, so today we have several chapters. I’ll list them: Chapter 1 is titled, “Why I Say This Community is Toxic,” which is my personal experience in the Scholar Cat Planet Knowledge Circle community. First, let me talk about the historical background. I met Scholar Cat around 2018 through the introduction of Teacher Zhang Xiaoyu. At first, we clicked really well, and soon became good friends. During that time, we basically communicated daily on WeChat, sharing a common hobby, and reading some very… well, mind-body-spirit related books. At that time, I felt it was a mutually supportive relationship, because, well, Scholar Cat’s community wasn’t like it is today, where everything seems to have an answer. We would ask each other questions, and I would ask him questions. It was in that state, and we discussed a book called The Guide to Living in the Present.
At that time, Scholar Cat was a very precious friend to me. He supported me during a very difficult period in my life, and we went out and played together. But around 2019, we started drifting apart because I noticed he began to move towards the path of “paying to win” (氪金)—spending a lot of money, buying luxury goods, or going to high-end hotels. In short, high-end consumption. At the same time, he also started focusing on the Zero Limit path.
For those who don’t know, I’ll explain Zero Limit later, but generally, this Zero Limit method isn’t my cup of tea. I didn’t criticize it much at the time; I just felt, “Yeah, I don’t like it. It’s too simple and too brainless.” I didn’t like this school of thought. More importantly, as I slowly interacted with him, I started to feel a strange sensation: we were no longer in a relationship of equal friends.
Because it seemed like every time we chatted, whether sitting down to eat or online, he seemed to know everything, understand everything, and could constantly output information, output his thoughts, his understanding, and try to inspire you, guide you, and help you open up your perspective, loosen your thinking. What is this? If this were a teacher and a student, if both of you agreed to enter such a hierarchical relationship, then of course, you can constantly listen to a teacher explain things to you. But if it’s friends, I think the foundation of friendship is that both are human—that both are, first and foremost, human. Which means both have flaws, both have weaknesses, and both have doubts. I think this is a basic commonality of being human. But chatting with Scholar Cat, the more and more I felt like he was a teacher, an old soul. He seemed to have very few doubts or vulnerabilities. I rarely heard him talk about any of his doubts or uncertainties. Of course, in his community, the nuances are even more subtle; he talks about his, say, his relationship experiences, which we will discuss later. But overall, he is someone who is not very… well, not showing weakness, not having any confusion. Slowly, I started to find it boring.
But in 2022, I saw that his official account had written a lot about paying to win, about how many people, under his guidance, had had very stimulating experiences through aggressive means. Yet, the overall style of the articles was very calm. It allowed you to feel, even amidst those very stimulating events, that “this makes sense,” and also feel that kind of cosmic great love. It felt like these two things combined created a huge contrast, which was also very interesting. So, when I frequently read his stuff, I have complex feelings: “Ugh, isn’t this nonsense?” But then I think, “Ah, it’s humorous, it makes sense,” and then I think, “Hmm, it’s going off the beaten path,” and then I think, “This person is very unique,” and then I feel a bit of envy, jealousy, and hatred. Sometimes I think, “Should I learn more about this?” And sometimes I feel, “Hmm, something might be wrong.” In short, I am constantly pulled back and forth between these complex emotions and thoughts.
Then, at a certain stage, I started thinking, why don’t I delve deeply into what he is talking about? On one hand, I wanted to reconnect with my old friend; on the other hand, I felt that perhaps the many things he talks about—things I don’t know, for example, I don’t have as much experience in finance as him—might be a new input, a new cognition for me, and truly help open something up for me. So, last year, I joined his community to get a close look at this person and his ideas. My background is in law and anthropology. As a legal professional, I have a principle I strongly adhere to.
In my knowledge system, if I don’t understand him, I should best presume that he is benevolent, presume that what he has is valuable, and then rationally view it, criticizing it only when necessary. So I still believe in this principle of presumption of innocence. As an anthropologist, I have curiosity, and I think the most important quality of an anthropologist is the willingness to immerse oneself in a culture. During the immersion process, of course, you temporarily set aside your critical thinking. For example, imagine you go to a primitive tribe. If you are constantly thinking, “What is this tribe all about?” you might find it difficult to truly understand this tribe from within, what it is like to be a member of this tribe. Of course, you can never truly become a member of that tribe; you still have your own nurtured background, your social background plays a huge role behind the scenes. But you try to put aside your preconceptions—the knowledge and insights you have gained previously—and allow yourself to truly be changed and permeated by that person or that community’s culture, and then look at yourself after being permeated.
It’s equivalent to the anthropologist studying an object using their own body, using their very genuine experience. So, of course, my entry into this community isn’t that high-brow; it’s not like I’m conducting an anthropological study. It’s just that I have this background. So I am very willing to truly assume that my previous ideas might have some limitations, some blind spots, and I want to experience, think, and act like a member of Scholar Cat’s community.
So, this experiment lasted for quite a long time—I think six or seven months. I kept myself in this mode of thinking and acting to see what kind of content was in Scholar Cat’s community. It actually covers three very important topics that everyone cares about. I heard people jokingly say that if you cover these three topics, any product or content you make will be bought, will go viral, and will make money. That’s “Get Rich, Get Lay, Don’t Die”—meaning get rich, and get laid (sex/love/intimacy), and then health.
Scholar Cat’s community covers these three topics: health, romance/marriage, and wealth. We can elaborate on these later. And these three topics are all underpinned by a grander cosmic view, a philosophy, or you could say a grand worldview, which is the Zero Limit cleansing method. So, you see, this structure is very deceptive. It places itself between very grand, very enlightened spiritual teachings and very bold, even gambler-like practices. The wealth, health, and romance—these all have a bit of that gambler-like quality, like they are trying to achieve something big with something small, or achieve cosmic-level rewards in a very clever way. That’s the general mindset. It bombards your nervous system every day with different chemical elements.
What are these chemical elements mainly? For example, adrenaline, which makes you very excited and anxious. Dopamine, which makes you addicted. But occasionally, there are very truthful or very soul-resonating feelings, like endorphins and oxytocin, that are at work. Do you feel like sometimes you are anxious, sometimes you are calm? This back-and-forth bombardment actually makes you very addicted. And this addiction constantly leads back to love and peace, finally to cleansing. But we still have to buy, buy, buy; we still have to eat, eat, eat; we still have to do something stimulating. This state of addiction is probably why many of us, including myself, and many of the community members want to check his Planet. So, next, let’s look at these topics one by one, and how they relate to this underlying worldview.
So, next I will divide it into several sections: one about Zero Limit, the second about paying to win, the third about 369 (the health diet method), and then about love and the overall community atmosphere. I will explain them in detail. First, although I have already made the judgment that this place is toxic, you can measure it yourself after hearing the details. So, those who are non-judgmental, you can leave now; you don’t have to listen to this episode. For those who are non-judgmental, you can enter this community. I should add that, of course, we practice Nonviolent Communication, and in some way, mind-body-spirit teachings force us to notice our habitual judgments, our complaints, our aggressive tendencies—like the habits of online trolls. But if you use it to review your own views and thoughts, and if it makes your naturally sharp, pointed thinking process dull, then…
You know, if you throw a “non-judgmental,” “cannot-be-judged,” or “don’t be too black-and-white” umbrella over things, who knows? When you throw this big umbrella, your sharp thoughts are immediately blurred, like a fog, and everything becomes like paste. I prefer to become very subjective and very extreme rather than dilute my views with that umbrella, with that paste-like fog.
First, Zero Limit. What kind of teaching is Zero Limit? It says that first, you must be 100% responsible for yourself. Everything you see is also your responsibility, even if someone else experiences pain—it is still within your own consciousness. So it must be cleansed by yourself. Pain is a replay of memory. So, for example, if you suffer some injustice in society, or if you, say, are robbed, or assaulted, it is still a memory of victimization playing back within yourself. So what you need to do is cleanse that memory. Everything else that goes wrong and causes pain is like that. You just need to take full responsibility for everything, even if someone hits you, you are responsible for it. Then you must delete, you must cleanse those memories. Similarly, others are your projections. So, this community likes to say NPC, which stands for Non-Player Characters. Just like when you play a game, only you are the real player. The other people who appear, even though they seem to be talking to you, their conversations are programmed. So, within this Zero Limit mindset, others are NPCs. Heh. How is this self-consistent? Are all of us NPCs? The general idea is that we are all NPCs. In my world, only I am real; I am 100% responsible for myself, and everyone else is my projection, an NPC.
So, even if others say something that hits me, or they hurt me in some way—for example, many people in the community were scammed—the person who was scammed is still an NPC. Ultimately, we are responsible for it ourselves, for returning it to ourselves, for cleansing the greed or the tendency to pick up small gains, or the fear within ourselves. How do you cleanse it? Zero Limit tells us that in some primitive tribe in Hawaii, they use this method to cleanse by constantly saying four phrases: Sorry, Please forgive, Thank you, I love you.
Or these four phrases are called PONO. There are many Zero Limit related products now. You see, this is truly an industry. You can buy, say, a notebook where you check off 1,000 times a day for cleansing. You constantly recite this, and it is also a form of meditation. Don’t you think so? Because whatever you do, even if you recite it 1,000 times, you can achieve a form of cleansing or enter a meditative state. You recite anything, it actually prevents your brain from thinking about other things temporarily. And you do it 1,000 times a day, or some people don’t do 1,000 times, but they constantly recite it in their minds. When you think of it, in your daily social life, when someone says something, you constantly think, “Sorry, please forgive, thank you, I love you.” Scholar Mom herself says that during her interactions with others, when she hears someone speak, she constantly silently recites these four phrases. So, this is a very highly self-consistent thought system. It is a closed system. It first tells you that everything is extremely, extremely your responsibility.
And other things, you don’t need to worry about them. You cleanse yourself, and the outside world will change. After you cleanse yourself, you will have… wealth comes, but he is also very smart. He says this cleansing is not just to make you rich or help you find an ideal partner, because if that’s the case, you still have a thought. So all thoughts must be cleansed. It looks very wise and profound.
Because when you cleanse everything to that absolute state of zero, it is indeed a grand and wide state that many practitioners or meditators pursue or experience. So it seems to be one level higher than other manifestation laws, because other manifestations say, “If you do these things, you will get these.” But the higher point of Zero Limit is that you must cleanse the thought that you will get those things. Even if you get them, you must cleanse that thought that the thing is good.
It is actually a bit like Vipassana. Vipassana ultimately says that you must zero out both the good and the bad. It actually has these ideas. So, this is any practice that might have some benefits. When it is used to the extreme, or when you use it brainlessly, it will produce some distorted things. For example, when using Zero Limit, or especially in Scholar Cat’s practice, if you have any doubts, you must cleanse that doubt. So, it is equivalent to it being unbeatable and never wrong. And you must constantly reinforce yourself and form a closed loop. Otherwise, you will keep doubting yourself. If you doubt, you cannot cleanse, unless you cleanse your own doubt. Do you understand this logic? So, if you have any dissatisfaction with the cleansing method, any doubt, any confusion, you…
And he adds a supplement: cleansing, or many current mind-body-spirit schools, have a bit of a contemptuous way of thinking. They feel that our society has always been like a pendulum. You see, our mainstream society or science, this modern society, it emphasizes rationality and downplays the body, the intuition, and the spirituality. Then, in the spiritual world, you swing to another extreme, where you constantly emphasize the body and intuition, and the signals of the universe, and you must submit to them. You must be brainless. He even thinks “brainless” is a good word. You must let go of your rational judgment, don’t analyze so much, don’t debate. Debate is also the biggest vice that prevents enlightenment. Don’t criticize, don’t think, don’t have those opposing forces. Look at the words I just said. If you change one to a softer one, without opposition, letting go of your thinking, letting go of your analysis, then it becomes a very reasonable, very soul-soothing meditation phrase. So, you see, hahaha, the same sentence, said with different tones, has different effects.
In short, in Zero Limit, don’t over-doubt, don’t over-think. Just chant like a fool. In Scholar Cat’s community, “chanting like a fool” is a good phrase. It means that even if you don’t understand what Zero Limit is at first, you constantly have doubts, but it doesn’t matter. You just repeat it like a fool. You repeat it to a certain degree, and you are truly brainwashed. You are truly changed, internalized, and permeated by his love, by those cosmic truths. So, you just keep repeating it.
For myself, I truly try to believe in this system, especially when I have many doubts. I think, “How come? I almost said, ‘Oh, I’m so unhappy, I’m so easily negative, complaining,’ because I questioned too much, because I like to dig into this matter, to figure it out to the root, and to research the origin of Zero Limit.”
For example, in India, not just in some primitive tribe in Hawaii, I really wanted to know how the primitive tribes did it. But the people who really practice Zero Limit don’t care how the primitive tribes did it; they just culturally appropriate and plunder it, and use it in a very fragmented way. But my personality is not like that; I cannot chant like a fool. So I struggled for several months. I tried to truly do it, but now I can finally announce that I can’t, haha. If this process helped me in any way, it helped me understand myself more clearly, and more clearly know how my path should be. For example, I truly don’t believe that negative thoughts are just cleansed when you chant them. When you keep chanting, it’s cleansed. This idea is too naive. Think about it: if your consciousness is a screen, a stage, and you constantly fill it with 1,000 Zero Limit cleansing mantras, after a while, of course, the negative thoughts will disappear, and you will feel how amazing it is—they really disappeared. But does that mean they are truly gone? For me, I still believe in the Jungian/Freudian idea: you actually have an unconscious. And now I have founded two communities: Circle in China, and Octopus Awakening. It also started to solidify. So I have left these two communities. And I am slowly exploring how to create more open and truly accommodating organizations for different opinions. I think my previous two communities were exploring this direction, but it seems that based on some structural reasons of the community, it still tends to homogenize. So this is a question mark that I keep holding. The third characteristic is consumerism becoming the driving force of manifestation. Look, in previous eras, it might be based on having to support the family, having to overcome the Great Depression. But now it is a crazy consumption, and market marketing, and various means, and various sales, and consumerism is rampant. And if you don’t criticize it, you can only follow it. Sometimes it even brings you benefits like honey, and you feel, “Hmm, I might still need some money,” or “I think it’s reasonable to spend on a five-star hotel or something.” “Others deserve it, why don’t I?” You start to feel that you must say these things. So consumerism is a big driving core of our contemporary mind-body-spirit.
So, why do you say mind-body-spirit is an industry? Well, if you look at the data, you know that in 2022, the entire mind-body-spirit industry, including yoga, meditation coaching, psychological counseling, various communities, and various more fringe spiritual retreats, totaled 43.7 billion US dollars.
You think about such a huge market, such a big slice of the pie. Everyone wants to share it, and everyone wants to ride on the imprint of this era, including what we might talk about in the future, about AI replacing human labor, about the fact that our life in this society has not much positive meaning. Capital likes these things? That’s combined with the social media we mentioned earlier, combined with the fact that our life is too uncertain, too without reliance.
Look, these things—capital, social media, the hope of certainty—will be generated. Mind-body-spirit, as an industry, constantly innovates, constantly replaces itself, self-repairs, and finds many of its own loopholes, and constantly optimizes itself to become a more self-consistent field. Look, our current astrology and human design can justify themselves, they cannot be falsified—these non-scientific things are particularly popular. I’m not saying science is good, it’s just that science, its premise is that it can be falsified. You can say today’s formula is wrong tomorrow, but astrology and human design can never be falsified. But what contemporary people need is something that cannot be falsified to give us a sense of certainty. Our life is too miserable, we are too uncomfortable, we need this.
I particularly like a quote from a YouTuber called Frog Dao Sheng. Because he himself was once a Christian, and then came out. And many people commented after his explanation, “If you don’t have a little faith, a little reliance, won’t you lose the meaning of life?” He has a quote that I particularly like: “If your spiritual world is too desolate, whether you believe in God or not is irrelevant.” In the end, it’s because you read too little. I think that’s it. You seek certainty, you seek meaning, the simplest way, the lazy way of not thinking, is to do astrology, to do human design.
If you read a little more, you can also find certain comfort in uncertainty, you can reconcile with uncertainty, and constantly overturn your ideas, constantly think. That is also a form of certainty. But this path is harder to walk. To be blunt, it is the path of the philosopher. The path of the philosopher requires privilege. What is the privilege of our current world? It is time, it is leisure time and energy. Most people, after working 996, where do they want to read books and think philosophically? They want to do some mind-body-spirit, and that can help them sleep. Then go to sleep, who goes to think? So that’s why mind-body-spirit is also a very good tool of governance. Everyone is busy working, and they casually use mind-body-spirit to soothe themselves. What a perfect social governance structure.
So, this leads to a very important point that I want to talk about: mind-body-spirit in the Chinese context is particularly toxic because it is completely depoliticized. I call it “Chinese-style mind-body-spirit capitalism.” What is politics? It is simple: the arrangement of public life. The politics we learned in primary school, it is called ideology. Why do we hate politics, don’t want to participate in politics? Because we haven’t had a positive experience of actively arranging public life. Even the smallest public life is politics, even if it is a neighborhood committee. But Chinese-style mind-body-spirit capitalism, it is based on consumption, and on love, it is completely depoliticized. Your family, and you return to the family, and you do wealth; politics is completely detached.
So, let’s go back to the development of spiritual earlier in the West. It has always been related to political demands. For example, in the peak period of the 60s, the hippie movement in the West, like The Beatles, and the Woodstock festival, they actually had demands, such as anti-war and social equality. In 2020, during the Trump-Biden election, there was even a spiritual writer called Marianne Williamson, who ran for president.
In a less extreme environment than China, actually, some schools of mind-body-spirit, because mind-body-spirit is a big concept, some are completely detached from politics, and some are willing to stand up to provide a new solution, a new idea for our politicization and political environment. For example, this Marianne, she feels that the current two factions are arguing too extremely, and they are very much in their own circles. We need a mind-body-spirit, a cosmic unity, but at the same time, we must have principles. Of course, she has a team. Of course, it’s not completely “everything is the best arrangement,” and she will stand up and say, “I hope mind-body-spirit can provide some solutions for politics.” So at least she has such an attempt. Although she eventually withdrew, hahaha.
But if we completely feel that mind-body-spirit is detached from politics, and from issues like feminism, environmentalism, labor, I think it is abnormal. It is not. If we belong to an interconnected society, then mind-body-spirit can naturally integrate with these things. But the version of mind-body-spirit that is most popular now, called “submission,” called “everything is the best arrangement,” called “everything is self-cleansing.” Wow, that is too easy to manage these people.
Okay, finally, how to cultivate critical thinking ability? Of course, this is a bit contradictory. If you have critical thinking ability, you don’t need me to teach you this chapter. But I will mention several points that I think are very important. First, read more books. You really need to read more books. Not just mind-body-spirit books, because I know there is a tendency in the mind-body-spirit field—if you look at your bookshelf, there are only mind-body-spirit books, then you really need to start reading more history, philosophy, more hard science, more empirical ones, and look for more independent news sources. And in hard science, if you are a liberal arts student and you don’t understand it, it doesn’t matter. You can flip through it, let your left brain get active. For a long time, your body is in it, your right brain is developed, but your left brain is not. This is a kind of overcorrection. Our mainstream society might be too developed in the left brain, and if you don’t understand it, it doesn’t matter. You can be permeated by its logic, its rigor, which is also a way to activate the left brain. And if you can slightly understand it with your brainpower, that’s even better.
And if you are really curious about quantum physics, you must read real quantum physics, not those fake spiritual quantum physics, pfft. Then you can also learn about basic philosophy, political science, anthropology, sociology, and logic, and linguistics—these things that understand the underlying structure of the human world. It will give you a framework, and you will know that when you hear a new thing, you can connect it with other knowledge. You won’t think, “Oh, this is amazing, it seems to be the truth.” You…
Our world has been around for thousands of years, so many philosophers, so many thinkers, step by step laid the foundation, and developed a little new idea based on the ideas of predecessors. How can you be so amazing that you can completely break away from their ideas and create your own new idea, and discover a cosmic truth? It’s not that simple. If you learn a little philosophy, history, and politics, you know these things are accumulated bit by bit. And besides reading these books, I also suggest everyone read useless books, because people in the personal growth circle love to read various technical, various… anyway, methods for self-improvement, it’s also an addiction. So you should read poetry, read sci-fi, read martial arts, read things that don’t improve yourself, to balance your information sources. Besides reading more books, the second point I want to talk about is colliding with people, debating more. Look, people in the mind-body-spirit field avoid debating because there is a kind of spiritual ego that says, “We are one,” “We are all unified,” “The world is harmonious.” Whatever you have, I can merge it into you, whatever you have, we can tolerate all emotions, all thoughts. So, in the end, this is a kind of enlightenment, a paste. It blurs things, and you feel that if you don’t think deeply, you feel that things can be compatible.
P—many things, you believe it can be compatible even if in the end, but the premise is that there is a huge rupture and many incompatibilities and dislikes. Only after debating, after fighting to the death, will they merge. This is Hegel’s idea of thesis and antithesis. First, you rupture, then you repair. Don’t be afraid of this rupture. People in the mind-body-spirit field are so afraid of rupture. How much are there? About the trauma of conflict. You pretend that you are especially harmonious, and you say, “I don’t mind, I, I don’t care if others criticize me, I don’t want to argue with people,” how noble you are, how elegant. I always feel that this is a band-aid. So, debating means solving it. It means you must first express it, like I am doing now, I am going crazy, I said a bunch of things. It doesn’t matter, don’t censor too much, just express it first. Of course, someone will disagree, and you can’t make everyone like you, and it’s okay if you are wrong, it’s okay if you are biased. Many of the things I said today are intentionally biased. I can’t make everything round, and I don’t want to do that. I just want to bring out my biased things, and welcome correction from me, welcome self-correction. I will slowly merge. Look at what I said today, I almost hate Scholar Cat. Of course, he has things that benefit me, this is not a justified hatred. I might slowly merge into it. Ugh, I don’t feel as angry as today. It might happen, but I can’t say, because it will happen. All these words I said today, I must say them. So you will find a very interesting thing: independent thinking is not achieved alone. Please remember this point: independent thinking is not achieved alone; it must be through collision. You must express it, and debate with people, discuss, explore, impact, friction, rupture, and then merge again. This is true independent thinking.
And this is the trap of our current mind-body-spirit generation: forcing every person back into their own small world, not caring about politics, not caring about others. Once your own logic is self-consistent, you don’t want to listen to other people’s logic, and you constantly self-cleanse, constantly self-reflect. You cannot recognize other aspects of society, you cannot view the world from the political perspective of other societies. It is a process that makes us lose the ability to think independently.
And the third point is that we must maintain a soft heart. What does soft mean? If you are narcissistic, you lock up your heart. Whether it is due to inferiority or arrogance, your soft part is locked up. So, to be soft means you will feel pain. Seeing a forest fire, seeing someone suffer, seeing a house collapse, you will feel pain. You just let that pain linger a little. Because I used to have a habit: when I see such painful news, I want to turn it off, I don’t want it to affect my mood for a long time. To a certain extent, this is the case. You cannot let it carry you away, and then you are depressed for the whole day, two days, three days. I think the method is to constantly learn how to adjust your nervous system so that it can coexist with this suffering, this pain in society, instead of just putting an ‘X’ on these pains and turning them off. Look, this is a very different path. When you close your heart, your heart becomes hard. That is your most precious thing; don’t defend yourself. So, one day, if you don’t feel pain when seeing these things, it’s not because you achieved enlightenment, or you achieved it, or you ascended to heaven. It’s because you cultivated it, you cultivated yourself to death.
If we say that very few people achieve enlightenment, this world is soft, and at the same time, it has a very strong place, and it can be regulated, but its hand is soft. It doesn’t lock itself up. When it sees separation and suffering, it still sheds tears. It’s not like, “I already know it is the universe’s operation principle, so these things won’t move me,” and I just cultivate myself, I cleanse myself.
Oh, this is also what they like to say: if there is war in the world, famine, strong suffering, hardship, then it must be that my unconscious, my inner self also has these things. And I must cleanse the desire or the memory and habit of fighting with others, fighting the war with others, then the world will be better. Pfft, damn it, I’m so angry. Right? So don’t cultivate it like this. If you cultivate it like this, you cultivate yourself to death. Ugh, this is also… I am not anxious, but my eunuch is anxious. Why be anxious? Look, if I say this pile of things, Scholar Cat will just smile calmly, he definitely won’t be angry, because anger is what a cultivated person would do. He would definitely say, “You are overthinking,” or look, you are like this suffering, he wouldn’t say anything, he would silently go back to cleanse it. And he would also make me cleanse it, if he still talks to me.
Anyway, today is my rambling self-talk, which is the end of my Deeply Loving Wealth. Why am I ending this blog? Because I feel that the atmosphere presented in the entire blog is a kind of… although I initially said I was an atheist, but slowly I have started to solidify my thinking. So, I think this podcast cannot continue. If I continue, I will still be talking about God, the universe, and so on. I think I’ve talked enough about those things, and those things definitely have some help. The many meditation audios before, many people feel they are helpful. If they are helpful, then they are helpful.
See you in a different Bubble.
Hahaha, hope that Bubble has more ventilation. Right? Because I cannot escape all bubbles. I just hope that whatever I do in the future is not so closed. By the way, if you don’t know, I have actually closed the Octopus Awakening community, so you can no longer join it. But Circle China is still there. I am not the main leader in it, but there are a few people I trust who are doing the main work, so I hope that if you are interested, you can play with Circle. It is relatively more open, and can accommodate different ideas. And if you like me, you can support me on Ai Fa Dian. Especially since I am in a transition period, I am brewing my new blog plan, or maybe other future projects. The hope is to break away from some of the drawbacks of the mind-body-spirit circle, but it might still accommodate some, because I have learned so much over the years, so I am still thinking about what form and what content it will be. So during this brewing period, I hope you can generously give me some financial support.
Recently, there hasn’t been too many cases, because I feel that in this period of change, I haven’t met new people. I hope to leave more white space for my own time, so that new ideas can emerge more freely. Just like I said earlier, the most luxurious and biggest privilege is time. And I am willing to give myself so much luxurious privilege. So if you are willing to support my process of independent thinking, I hope you can support me on Ai Fa Dian or directly find my donation QR code on the WeChat official account, and you can support me after any article.
Speaking of this, I think my current view of wealth is not just how many luxury goods you can buy, or how much liquidity you have today. I think it is being able to afford to be disliked—this is the greatest freedom. I can afford being disliked, I can afford public speaking—meaning I can afford to express my true views in public. I think this is the greatest wealth, including the time I just mentioned. Okay, so that’s all for today’s content. See you in the future. Bye-bye.
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the final episode of Deeply Loving Wealth (or Deeply Loving Finance). I’m JS Jing Shu. As for what the future blog or other content will be, I’ll save that for the next episode—that is, the first episode of the new podcast. Since this is the last one, I’m just going to go a little crazy. I’m giving up on being Lin Blogger’s face, or whatever. I’m just done with it.

The outcome of merely “studying” without “applying” (which is the reality for most Chinese students) is that even after more than a decade, they are still studying and still useless (this is the reality for most Chinese students).

The reason we “study for a lifetime” yet insist on “never applying it for a lifetime” is because we are afraid of making mistakes. When we make mistakes in childhood, they often lead to punishment. In adulthood, even if there is no punishment from others, there is still the self-deprecation and embarrassment caused by making a mistake. Therefore, many people avoid errors “at all costs.” However, we must know that the process of acquiring knowledge cannot be separated from trial and error. Without trial and error, comprehensive and genuine progress is impossible. So, you must know that making mistakes is normal, and it is even indispensable. When doing something, making mistakes is inevitable. If you are doing something and there isn’t a single mistake, then you aren’t doing something—you are dreaming.

Pursue wealth, not money or status. Wealth refers to assets that continue to earn money for you while you sleep. Money is the way we convert time into wealth. Status is the position you hold in the social hierarchy. Note - Location 321 Social status is a zero-sum game.
Relying on renting out your time is impossible to get rich. You must own equity (a part of the company’s ownership) to achieve financial freedom.
One way to acquire wealth is to provide society with something it needs but cannot obtain, and then achieve scale.
To acquire wealth, you must fully utilize the leverage effect. Business leverage comes from capital, labor, and products whose marginal cost of replication is zero (code and media).
There is a large number of robots available for us to use for free. To improve thermal efficiency and save space, these robots are concentrated in data centers. Use them.
Study microeconomics, game theory, psychology, persuasion, ethics, mathematics, and computer science.
Set a bold personal hourly rate and strictly enforce it. If the cost saved by solving a problem is less than your hourly rate, ignore the problem; if the cost of outsourcing a task is less than your hourly rate, choose to outsource it.
What you truly want is wealth. Wealth is an asset that can make money for you even while you sleep. Wealth can be factories and robots that produce. Wealth can be computer programs that serve clients day and night. Wealth can also be money in the bank that is invested in other assets or businesses.
To make money in society, you must provide society with something it needs but cannot obtain. If society has already created the needed products and services, you will no longer be needed.
Through the internet, everyone can find their audience. As long as you engage in unique self-expression online, you have the opportunity to spread happiness, accumulate wealth, create products, and start businesses.[78]
The starting point is not important; the action itself is what matters. Therefore, adhering to moral standards is not easy.
If you do not hold company equity, the correlation between personal input and return will be very strong. Almost all salaried jobs, even high-paying professions like lawyers or doctors, require time input to earn corresponding income.
The first is labor leverage, which means having others work for you. Labor leverage is one of the oldest forms of leverage, but in modern society, its effectiveness is not the best.[1] I even think it is the most outdated form of leverage. Because managing others is a very complex and challenging job that requires superb leadership skills, the manager might end up being abandoned by their followers and devoured by their subordinates.[78]
Capital is the second, relatively better form of leverage. Capital leverage is using money to expand the influence of decisions.[1] Capital is a more modern form of leverage, and utilizing it has a certain difficulty, requiring certain skills. In the 20th century, people gained astonishing wealth by using capital leverage. Capital leverage was the main form of leverage in the 20th century.
And things like programming, writing books, recording podcasts, tweeting, and filming videos do not require permission from anyone. It can be seen that new leverage acts like an equalizer, greatly narrowing the gap between people and making society more equal.[78] For example, every excellent software developer now has a large group of robots working for them. After writing the code, these robots start working and earning money for the developer even while they sleep.[78] Relying on renting out your time can never lead to wealth.
One major goal of life should be to control your own time. The ideal job is one that utilizes the leverage effect. In this work model, you can control your time and be responsible for your output and results. If you bring a miraculous turning point to a company by providing excellent solutions, you will certainly receive financial rewards. Especially if others don’t even know how you did it, they must continuously pay you to continue providing that product or service. And the reason you can do this is because of your obsession, skill, or talent.
One other point that benefits me: I value freedom above all else. The freedom I speak of is diverse: the freedom to do what you want to do, the freedom not to do what you don’t want to do, the freedom from being influenced by self-emotions or external factors, etc. Freedom is the value I cherish the most.
To face reality, you must let go of the self, eliminate self-consciousness, forget self-judgment, and calm self-emotions. Although humans are advanced animals, the existence of emotional self-consciousness brings rumination, allowing certain desires to blind our eyes, making us unable to see reality clearly, and thus leading us to rashly judge “how the world should be.” This situation often occurs, especially when mixing political demands with business issues.
The difficulty lies in seeing the truth clearly. To see the truth clearly, you must escape the self, because the self does not want to face the truth. The weaker the self, the fewer the restrictions on its reactions, and the lower the obsession with the desired outcome, the easier it is to see reality clearly.
The craving for a beautiful reality blinds the perception of the real world. What is called suffering is the inability to continue ignoring the facts.
Note - Location 1130 The more you crave to solve a problem in a specific way, the less likely you are to see the facts clearly.
Without thinking, you won’t have outstanding business ideas, nor can you make correct judgments. I encourage everyone to spend at least one day a week thinking (preferably two days, because even if you allocate two days, it might end up being one).
Only a relaxed brain can generate great ideas. A person who feels immense pressure, is bogged down in paperwork, is constantly running around, and is stressed out cannot think. Therefore, you must make time for thinking.[7]
Almost all biases are designed to help people make quick judgments when information is incomplete. For important decisions, set aside memory and identity, and focus on the problem itself.
Bookmark - Location 1244
If it is difficult to choose, then the answer is negative.
The difference between people is not “educated” and “uneducated,” but “likes reading” and “dislikes reading.”
Read classic works in mathematics, science, and philosophy. Don’t read bestsellers, don’t watch the news. Avoid joining any so-called “book clubs,” avoid pursuing any social conformity. Place truth above social conformity.[11]
The reality is that life is a single-player game. A person is born alone, dies alone, and interprets everything in the world alone. Your memories belong only to you. Before you are born, no one cares; after you leave the world, no one cares. You exist in the world for only a few decades; life is a single-player game.
Essentially, the process of life is replacing bad habits formed unintentionally with well-cultivated good habits, striving to become a happier person. Your happiness index ultimately depends on your habits and the people you spend the most time with.
The more secrets you have, the lower your sense of happiness.[11]
The purpose of the news is to make people feel anxious and angry. But the science, economics, education, and conflict trends behind the news have positive significance. You must maintain a good state of mind and an optimistic attitude.[11]

When dealing with risk management, there are many useful tools and methods that can help you reduce financial risks and better manage your assets. Here are some risk management tools and methods worth considering:
Insurance: Purchasing appropriate insurance is the most basic and important risk management tool. Health insurance, car insurance, property insurance, life insurance, etc., can provide you with economic support and protection when accidents or disasters occur.
Diversified Portfolio: When investing, spreading funds across different asset classes, such as stocks, bonds, real estate, and cash, helps to diversify risk. Such a diversified portfolio can reduce losses when specific assets perform poorly.
Emergency Savings Fund: Establishing an emergency savings fund is used to cope with sudden emergencies and unexpected expenses. It is usually recommended to save an amount equivalent to three to six months of living expenses as an emergency reserve.
Stop-Loss Strategy: In investing, setting a stop-loss point is a common risk management method. By setting a price point, assets are automatically sold when the asset price falls to a certain degree, thus avoiding further losses.
Professional Financial Advisor: Seeking the help of a professional financial advisor or wealth planner can help you formulate personalized risk management strategies and make reasonable plans based on your goals and risk tolerance.
Long-Term Investment: Long-term investment is usually more stable than short-term speculation because it can smoothly handle market fluctuations and achieve more stable returns through the accumulation of time.
Healthy Lifestyle: Maintaining a healthy lifestyle helps reduce medical costs and health risks. Regular physical examinations and maintaining healthy eating habits can reduce the possibility of illness.
Compliance with Laws and Regulations: Adhering to laws and regulations, including traffic rules and building safety standards, can reduce many potential property and liability risks.
Education Planning: Planning for your children’s education in advance helps to distribute the pressure of future educational expenses.
Debt Management: Managing personal debt ensures that the debt burden is reasonable and does not exceed your capacity to bear it.
In summary, risk management is a crucial part of personal financial planning. By using appropriate tools and methods, you can better protect your and your family’s financial security and plan for the future more effectively.

The DCA strategy includes the following key points: What exactly is the asset? How long is the long-term horizon? How long is the regular interval? What is the minimum amount invested each time?
2 The securities trading market is the ninth great wonder of the world.
Highlight(yellow) - Location 197
People always think that “choosing stocks” is a very difficult thing—actually, it’s not difficult at all! Because the so-called “difficulty” is entirely caused by inertial thinking. In reality, it is merely the result of people being unwilling or afraid to use the simplest, most direct, crude, and effective method. This method is so simple, so unbelievably simple: simply choose the stocks that everyone in the market favors the most.
3 Are there truly investment assets that only rise and never fall?
Highlight(yellow) - Location 260
Therefore, Warren Buffett always recommends that ordinary people buy the S&P 500 index fund—in China, the corresponding asset for the S&P 500 is the CSI 300 index fund. The advantage of index funds is that they are essentially equivalent to “following the market.” You don’t have to bet on the luck of a single company; instead, you bet on the luck of the entire nation, or the luck of the entire world—in any case, in the long run, the scale of the human economy is constantly growing. Look, as long as it is long-term, it suddenly stops being a gamble, because in the long run, risk can actually be diluted to the point of near elimination.
4 The only correct way for ordinary people to invest.
Highlight(yellow) - Location 359
People who “go all in” (put everything on the line) cannot endure pain for too long—in fact, no one can endure pain long-term. This has absolutely nothing to do with so-called “strength.” From another perspective, this isn’t foolishness; it’s merely ignorance. After a month, or two months, or three months of pain, even when looking back, when they feel they are about to get through it, that is, around the sixth month (or slightly before), many people will exit for various reasons—in the trading market, this behavior is called “cutting the meat” (or “cutting losses”). Look, the leeks (investors) cut themselves, and what they cut off is bloody meat.

Requirement Analysis Analyze the needs of the target users and determine the core functions and features that the APP needs to implement. This requires user research, competitor analysis, etc.
Information Architecture and Interaction Design Based on the requirements and user research, design the APP’s information architecture, determine the interface flow and interaction logic. Common design tools include Axure, Sketch, etc.
Visual Design Conduct the visual design of the APP, including interface style, icons, colors, fonts, etc. Common tools include Photoshop, Illustrator, etc.
Frontend Development Develop the APP interface using frontend development frameworks, such as React Native, Flutter, etc. Proficiency in languages like JavaScript, Dart is required.
Backend Development Develop the APP’s backend business logic, providing interfaces and data support. Uses server languages like PHP, Java, Python, and databases like MySQL, MongoDB.
Testing Conduct functional testing, interface testing, performance testing, security testing, etc., during the development process to ensure APP quality. Tools used include Appium, JMeter, etc.
Deployment and Operations Deploy the APP to the App Store and Google Play, and conduct continuous monitoring and later optimization/upgrades. Uses platforms like Firebase.
Therefore, modern APP development requires interdisciplinary collaboration and mastery of various professional tools to create a product that users love. This process requires the concerted efforts of designers, developers, and testers.

If you yourself are part of the tide, how can you see the direction of the tide? You can only maintain skepticism forever. Ask yourself: what words can I not say? Why?

content: The prerequisite for robbery is that there must be something to steal; the prerequisite for kidnapping and demanding ransom is that the hostage must have the financial capacity to pay the ransom. As the Law of Blood Payment (or Law of Life Compensation) states, the value of the hostage’s life is determined by the willingness and ability of the parties to pay the ransom. Under conditions of equal risk and cost, the richer the hostage, and the wealthier the target of the robbery, the higher the profit from the kidnapping and robbery. Conversely, the poorer the target of the robbery and kidnapping, the lower the profit from the robbery. If the profit is so low that it is not worth the effort, the bandits cannot proceed.

If one could ride a time machine back to the past, no matter which era, one thing would remain unchanged: “misfortune comes from the mouth” (or “words bring disaster”). You must be careful about what you say.
Words that seem harmless can bring you great trouble.
Today, saying that the Earth revolves around the Sun is utterly commonplace. But if you said that in 17th-century Europe, you would be in serious trouble.
Galileo said those words, and as a result, he faced judgment from the religious court.
Nerds/Bookworms are the kind of people who get into trouble like that.
They wear unpopular clothes and speak inappropriate words.
They feel they have expressed the correct viewpoint, but in reality, they attract trouble.
The power of custom is not enough to restrain them.
The norm of history seems to be that people in any era firmly believe in some absurd things.
Their beliefs are very strong; as long as someone shows even a slight doubt, they will attract great trouble. Is our era different? If you have read a little history, you know the answer is almost certainly “no difference.”
Even if there is that tiny possibility, for the first time in history, that all the beliefs of our era are correct, it is due to astonishing coincidence, not because we have truly found the correct direction.
When one thinks that what we assert with certainty now is seen as absurd by people in the future, how can one not be amazed!
summary:
If one could ride a time machine back to the past, no matter which era, one thing would remain unchanged: “misfortune comes from the mouth” (or “words bring disaster”). You must be careful about what you say.

Words that seem harmless can bring you great trouble.

Today, saying that the Earth revolves around the Sun is utterly commonplace. But if you said that in 17th-century Europe, you would be in serious trouble.
title: Throughout all dynasties and generations, ancient and modern, domestic and international, it is all disaster springing from the mouth.

If you truly believe it, and for anything that disagrees with society, you don’t even dare to think about it, immediately giving up your own viewpoint, that is when the real problem occurs.

content:
First, we can look at how people get into trouble because of what they say.
Only if two conditions are met simultaneously.
The first condition is that the words cannot be said;
The second condition is that they are correct, or seem likely to be correct and are worth further discussion. If the second condition is not met, in most cases, you won’t have trouble.
If you say that 2+2 equals 5, or that the average height of a citizen in Pittsburgh is three meters, you won’t have any issues. These obviously incorrect statements might be taken as a joke, or worse, as proof that you are crazy, but they certainly won’t anger anyone.
Statements that anger others are those that people might believe.
I hypothesize that the most infuriating statements are those believed to be telling the truth. If Galileo said that the people of Padua are three meters tall, he would only be regarded as a quirky, mad scientist.
But, when he said that the Earth revolves around the Sun, the nature of it was completely different.
The Church knew that this kind of statement would make people start thinking.

In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the development of the socio-economy and population growth, farmers’ demand for land increased. However, the uneven distribution of land and the heavy burden of taxes made it impossible for many farmers to maintain a livelihood. Therefore, they began seeking ways to improve their lives, such as temporary registration (jiji), wandering/migrating (youyu), or engaging in maritime commerce (xiahai jingshang) 12.
In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the corruption of officials and lax supervision, the management of the Yellow Registers and travel permits became chaotic and riddled with loopholes. Phenomena such as fraudulent registration (maoji), fake household registration (jiaji), and privately manufactured travel permits were frequently observed, causing the household registration system to lose its regulatory power 12.
In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to causes such as natural disasters, warfare, and epidemics, many regions experienced sharp population decline, missing household registrations, and land abandonment. This caused the data in the Yellow Registers and travel permits to severely mismatch the actual situation, making it impossible to reflect the true population dynamics 1.

As a dynasty moves from its middle period towards its late years, it is often accompanied by a series of characteristic changes. Here are some common changes:
Political Instability and Power Struggles: As time passes, the dynasty’s governance often experiences instability and power struggles. Political corruption, unfair official appointments, and the phenomenon of vying for power may intensify, leading to internal political instability and chaos.
Territorial Retreat and War Challenges: In its late years, the dynasty may face territorial shrinkage, losing control over certain regions. External forces may launch wars, challenging the dynasty’s territory. This can lead to the weakening of the nation’s military strength and a reduction in territory.
Economic Decline and Fiscal Difficulties: The late years of a dynasty are often accompanied by economic recession and financial hardship. Reduced tax revenue and insufficient fiscal income to support national operations lead to rising prices, heavier taxation, and social poverty. Economic difficulties may result in social instability and public dissatisfaction.
Social Unrest and Popular Uprisings: With the arrival of the late dynasty, social unrest and popular uprisings may occur frequently. Phenomena such as peasant rebellions, waves of migration, and local fragmentation (or regional warlordism) may intensify, posing a serious threat to the stability of the central government. These uprisings and unrest are often a strong resistance against government corruption, exploitation, and oppression.
Cultural Decline and Knowledge Atrophy: The late dynasty is often accompanied by cultural decline and intellectual atrophy. Fields such as academic research, literary arts, and technological innovation may be negatively affected, and the social cultural life and knowledge inheritance are suppressed.
These changes are common characteristics of a dynasty’s late years, but the specific situation varies depending on the history, region, and specific dynasty. The late years of a dynasty are often a stage of decline and demise, bearing obvious signs of recession and collapse.
summary:
As a dynasty moves from its middle period towards its late years, it is often accompanied by a series of characteristic changes. Here are some common changes:

Territorial Retreat and War Challenges: In its late years, the dynasty may face territorial shrinkage, losing control over certain regions. External forces may launch wars, challenging the dynasty’s territory. This can lead to the weakening of the nation’s military strength and a reduction in territory.
title: What are the defining changes as a dynasty moves from its middle phase to its final years?

content:
There are multiple factors that can lead to the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty:
Negligence and Political Corruption of Rulers: At the end of a dynasty, issues of negligence and political corruption among rulers often intensify. Phenomena such as official corruption, bribery, and improper appointments lead to a decline in government efficiency, making it unable to effectively manage the national finances and economy. Such corrupt practices weaken fiscal revenue, resulting in financial difficulties.
Excessive Taxation and Intensified Exploitation: To fill the fiscal deficit, the imperial court often increases the burden of taxes and the collection of other tribute goods. This places a heavy burden on farmers and merchants, leading to hindered economic development, decreased productivity, and even sparking social discontent and protests.
Obstruction of Domestic and International Trade and Market Contraction: The late dynasty often faces issues of obstructed domestic and international trade. Internal unrest and external wars lead to the interruption of transportation and trade routes, affecting the circulation of goods and the development of the market economy. Market contraction reduces commercial activities, further exacerbating the economic decline.
Decline in Agricultural Production and Frequent Disasters: Agriculture is the foundation of a dynastic economy, but at the end of a dynasty, agricultural production often declines. Factors such as long-term warfare, land abandonment, and peasant uprisings lead to a decrease in agricultural productivity. Simultaneously, natural disasters such as drought, floods, and locust plagues occur frequently, resulting in reduced or destroyed crops, further weakening the economic foundation.
Social Instability and Warfare Affecting Investment and Development: The late dynasty is often accompanied by social instability and warfare. Turbulent situations, such as internal rebellions, external threats, and peasant uprisings, hinder investment and development. Merchants and landlords may be reluctant to invest in economic development or transfer their assets, leading to a decline in economic vitality.
These factors interact to cause the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty. The combination of rulers’ negligence and political corruption, excessive taxation and exploitation, trade obstruction, agricultural decline, and social upheaval collectively leads to economic distress and fiscal collapse.
summary:
There are multiple factors that can lead to the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty:

Negligence and Political Corruption of Rulers: At the end of a dynasty, issues of negligence and political corruption among rulers often intensify. Phenomena such as official corruption, bribery, and improper appointments lead to a decline in government efficiency, making it unable to effectively manage the national finances and economy. Such corrupt practices weaken fiscal revenue, resulting in financial difficulties.
title: Why are the late years of a dynasty often accompanied by economic decline and fiscal difficulties?

content: Before ascending the throne, Zhu’s forces were always the “Army of Benevolence and Righteousness” (Renyi Zhi Shi), and Zhu himself was always a model of practicing the “King’s Way” (Wang Dao). Consequently, the people willingly submitted their hearts and allegiance. Who would have thought that after conquering the realm and incorporating the entire populace into his cage, he would transform from being generous and benevolent to being harsh and cruel, raising the whip and the butcher’s knife to slaughter the world, massacring meritorious officials, and becoming a demonic king that made everyone tremble with fear? In fact, it was not Zhu Yuanzhang’s nature that changed, but the circumstances. Before ascending the throne, he sought support from various social classes; he needed to gain their backing. After ascending the throne, the common people had become the cattle and sheep under his pastoral care, and naturally, he was happy to command them forward with the butcher’s knife and the whip.

content:
Work is the essence of human life, but it is not the purpose of human life. The author argues that from the moment humans appeared on Earth, they have had to engage in labor to acquire resources and energy, thereby sustaining survival and reproduction. However, work is not the sole meaning of human existence; humans also have other needs and pursuits, such as leisure, entertainment, social interaction, and creativity. The author calls on us not to treat work as a religion (or faith), but rather as a means to better enjoy life.
The form and meaning of work change as human civilization evolves. The author traces the historical transformation of human labor, from primitive society, agricultural society, industrial society, to modern society. He points out that different social forms and economic systems have different definitions and requirements for work. In primitive society, people did not have the concept of “work”; they simply labored to meet basic survival needs. In agricultural society, people began to settle down and cultivate land, forming land ownership and class systems. In industrial society, people were alienated into “tool people” (or “cogs in the machine”), working tirelessly for economic growth. In modern society, people have greater expectations and challenges regarding work, hoping to gain a sense of value and achievement through it.
Scarcity economics is the root cause of people’s overworking. The author believes that the “scarcity mindset” prevalent in modern society makes people worry that resources are insufficient, thus striving hard to work to acquire more wealth and material goods. However, this mindset ignores that human demand for resources is finite, and resources themselves are not fixed or unchanging. The author proposes the concept of “Abundance Economics” (or “Sufficiency Economics”), arguing that humans should learn from primitive society how to control desires, be content with existing resources, and expand the availability of resources through innovation and collaboration.
Automation technology will bring new opportunities and challenges to humanity. The author predicts that in the future, robots will replace humans in performing most repetitive and low-skilled jobs, which will lead humans to face crises of unemployment and uselessness. But at the same time, this will also bring new possibilities to humanity, giving people more time and space to develop fields they are interested in and skilled at, and creating more valuable and meaningful work. The author suggests that we should rethink the question of “what makes us human,” and transition from being “tool people” to being “Human Beings.”
summary: Work is the essence of human life, but it is not the purpose of human life. The author argues that from the moment humans appeared on Earth, they have had to engage in labor to acquire resources and energy, thereby sustaining survival and reproduction. However, work is not the sole meaning of human existence; humans also have other needs and pursuits, such as leisure, entertainment, social interaction, and creativity. The author calls on us not to treat work as a religion (or faith), but rather as a means to better enjoy life.
title: The Significance of Work: Human Transformation from Prehistory to the Future
