content:
Many people’s correct decisions come to an end without a clear outcome: Asking someone who has only ridden a bicycle, “Is Li Auto worth buying?” Asking someone who has never profited from equity investment, “Should you become a Meihua LP?”… Often, the right or wrong decision is determined by the person you consult. One way of giving bad advice is by saying, “It’s for your own good.” When encountering people inferior to you, you must firmly hold your beliefs. When encountering people similar to you, you must doubt your beliefs. When encountering people superior to you, you must negate your beliefs.
The only true asset a person possesses is time. The only important strategy is how you use your time. For valuable things, don’t worry about the price; for worthless things, don’t waste time. Whether your decision-making is based on a price mindset or a value mindset will result in vastly different outcomes. Entrepreneurship is like building with LEGOs; time is often spent not on studying the blueprints, but on searching for the pieces. The three things founders must always focus on are: finding people, finding money, and finding direction.
If an entrepreneur does not thoroughly reflect on a lesson, that lesson will be repeated over and over until you completely learn it. People teach people—a hundred times you might not learn it; things teach people—once you will learn it. What convinces a person is not preaching, but a firm, unyielding stance (a “South Wall”).
The opportunity for the poor to turn their fortunes around is placing a heavy stake. If you don’t have the quantity of chips, you must have the multiples; betting evenly is unlikely to lead to a turnaround. Your heavy stakes include money, time, energy, and loyalty. The so-called “first pot of gold” is the amount that allows you to climb the first step. This society is both realistic and cruel; money flows toward those who don’t lack it, and hardship is left for those who can endure it.
Many people’s lives are better than before, but they haven’t become as happy as they imagined. Human happiness is determined in three layers: the first by the senses, the second by dopamine, and the third by endorphins. Most people have the first layer, but most people lack the third. What truly determines the degree of a person’s happiness is how much dopamine is secreted in the second layer. From a dopamine perspective, having existing stock is boring; only gaining increments is interesting. Don’t rely on old capital; establish new achievements. Only with increments will there be dopamine, and only then will there be more happiness. For an investor, a cross-industry stand-up comedy show is an increment.
“Being the least wrong” is a game: “If the level is equivalent, be the one who makes the fewest mistakes.” Similarly, entrepreneurship is a game where, if the strategy and tactics are clear, you are the one who is more efficient or more frugal. Among the new car powerhouses, Li Auto makes the fewest mistakes in the same areas, which wins it a large majority.
An entrepreneur’s evolution requires leaving the comfort zone and entering the adaptation zone. Whoever suffers, changes; whoever changes, adapts; whoever adapts, benefits. The most effective way to leave the comfort zone is to take others as a mirror to reflect your own problems. Ordinary people like to hear pleasant words, just as children like to eat candy—sweet but useless. Experts like to hear unpleasant words, just as adults like to drink tea—bitter but detoxifying.
Don’t pull people onto the entrepreneurial path; instead, attract those who need you on the entrepreneurial path. If you pull people into entrepreneurship, you must make a promise. A promise gives certainty, and certainty triggers laziness and bad behavior.
Smart people find fools as opponents and experts as friends. This is contrary to human nature, but conforms to common sense. Dumb people find experts as opponents and fools as friends. This conforms to human nature, but violates common sense.
A person has three lives: one at birth, one when mental power emerges, and one when cognitive awakening occurs. Mental power and cognition are the Governing and Conception Meridians of the entrepreneur; only by opening them can one truly be invincible. Success without the growth of mental power and cognition is more terrifying than failure, because eventually, time will revert luck-driven success back to its original state. Climbing the social ladder is difficult; falling requires only a very short time.
Humans are naturally double-standard animals. Understanding the double standards of others and overcoming one’s own double standards is a lifelong cultivation—it is a painful spiritual discipline that distinguishes whether a person can truly be objective, honest, and empathetic.
Charlie Munger believes there are 5 items for a happy life:
Don’t overconsume; don’t exceed your capacity. Engage in prudent investment. Stay away from toxic people and toxic activities. Maintain lifelong learning. Do more things that involve delayed gratification. Otherwise, you will need to possess extremely good luck! The master believes that even ordinary things contain subtle complexities. Most people ultimately expect to have extremely good luck, spending time burning incense and praying to Buddha, choosing to enter the temple in evolution and business.
Money that is raised is easily spent; only money earned in the market is worth spending. A first-class entrepreneur’s ability to make money is always far greater than their ability to raise money. 95% of founders’ spending ability must be honed through painful experiences; when you don’t know how to spend, being frugal is very important. Many founders spend money on the back of the knife, or even the hilt, meaning they haven’t spent it on the blade itself.
That’s just how humans are. Even if barely, as long as you are slightly ahead of the opponent in some aspect, a state of flow will emerge, and you can even exert 120% or 150% of your power. You must grit your teeth and insist on leading, fully utilizing the “Great Tree Principle”: in a forest, the taller the tree, the more sunlight it receives. Through photosynthesis, the tree grows faster.
In any company, fence-sitters and opportunists are the majority. When you are struggling or making mistakes, it is normal for them to remain neutral and observe. If you use a single, absolute loyalty-driven value system, you will push them toward your side as your opponents.
The unwritten rules of entrepreneurial socializing are: only screen, don’t educate. Changing others is a huge internal drain; changing yourself is growth. Both favorable circumstances and adversity are reflections of the inner self. If you cling to them, if your heart is moved, they are adversity for you; if you let go, if your heart is still, everything is favorable.
Moving toward the high places means moving toward a higher dimension, not just to gain more ability, but to acquire more information. In a higher dimension, the speed, density, and accuracy of information you possess are completely different; it becomes your cognitive depth. With cognitive depth, you can down-dimension, achieve compatibility, and serve the users you can serve—this is the logic of making money.
“True light is not the absence of darkness, but the state of never being obscured by darkness. A true hero is not the absence of humble sentiment, but the state of never being subjugated by humble sentiment.” — A passage I deeply appreciate.

Comment seeding/driving traffic (评论引流) can be traced back to the blog era, where people would mass-comment on other websites. The username and the comment content served as advertisements. By commenting on hundreds or thousands of websites, one could continuously bring in a steady stream of traffic.
A well-known expert in the blogger community, Lu Songsong, insisted on commenting under various blog posts back then, which provided significant help to his later traffic and fame.
In the era of self-media (self-publishing/personal branding), this method is still effective, and the key is its simplicity—anyone can do it.
Taking the popular low-cost online courses of recent years as an example: Register a D Account (D 音号), change the username to your business name, and ensure the username and avatar are enticing—making people want to click immediately. Pre-follow several hundred knowledge bloggers, and whenever they publish content, comment on it first.
Don’t post advertisements, as they might be deleted. The comment content can simply follow a template. When commenting on knowledge-based bloggers, you can use phrases like: “Got it,” “This is truly useful, thanks for sharing,” “Nice, saved it,” etc.
For an ordinary video, a baseline view count of three to five hundred is standard, but viral hits reaching tens to millions of views are also common. With your username and avatar exposed countless times, some people will inevitably click on them. By posting business-related videos and leaving your personal WeChat in the signature, people will add you as a friend daily, resulting in a very stable conversion rate.
The specific steps for beginners are as follows:
Find a niche industry that has high conversion rates, is a necessity (high demand), and has a wide market. Organize relevant materials. Register a D Account, modify the username and avatar, post a few business-related videos, and use the signature to guide people to add your WeChat. Follow 100+ quality peers and comment blindly—the more the better.

content:
Tycoons pursue high quality and are hard to fool. Middle class pursues cost-effectiveness and is meticulous/penny-pinching. Idiots act on instinct and are easily fooled.
Instinct includes: seeking cheap deals, emotional reactions, fear of missing out (FOMO), love of getting a bargain…
Live streaming e-commerce primarily relies on short video traffic generation.
What kind of short video is more attractive?
Bankruptcy clearance sales, middle-aged people shedding tears… This perfectly matches the greed for cheap deals and emotionality of the lower class.
Recently, my brother has been scrolling through short videos and seeing many similar videos. The tactics are all the same: “Business can’t go on,” “Bankrupt,” “Loss-making clearance sale.”
These videos with the same tactics are posted repeatedly, grinding the intelligence of the viewers into the ground.
Through short videos, driving traffic to the live stream room works extremely well.
If the live streaming is proficient, you can also run paid traffic (ad spend). If the return on investment (ROI) is greater than 1, you can amplify the operation, and the returns will be considerable.
If the ROI is even, you aren’t losing; at least you gain a fan. If the ROI is slightly negative, as long as the number of fans increases significantly, you still aren’t losing.
Setting up the live stream room at zero cost: Use a green screen setup and find material from a book wholesale supplier to use as the video background.
There is absolutely no technical complexity throughout the process; OBS + Live Companion is enough to handle it.
The product sources for the live stream room are very simple; you can find them directly from curated alliances—zero cost, zero inventory, earning commissions.
Many of the books are priced like cabbage (very cheap), making the traffic generation effect excellent.
Sellers, in order to boost sales and have more people help sell the goods, will offer low prices to drive volume. This is a standard operation.
When you enter the product page, you will find packages at different prices. The low price is the traffic driver, and the high price is the profit driver. As long as enough people buy, the profit from the high-priced items is enough to cover the losses from the low-priced items, and there will still be a surplus.
Use “brain-dead” videos to attract “brain-dead” viewers into the live stream room. Use paid traffic to boost the live stream room’s data. Use “cabbage-priced” products to attract “leeks” (easy targets/consumers). Use profit-driven products to increase revenue.
With a live stream room like this, how will the sales be?
Monthly sales of 50,000 units+
The overall operational framework is just like this; there is no technical complexity.
One background image, randomly copy some popular inspirational quotes, and you can create a video in minutes.
Even these “lame/trash” videos can get over ten thousand views….
The only drawback is that 97% of the traffic is system-pushed. Once you post content from other fields, the views immediately drop to a few hundred.

content: One form of leverage is labor—other humans working for you. It is the oldest form of leverage, and actually not a great one in the modern world. [1] I would argue this is the worst form of leverage that you could possibly use. Managing other people is incredibly messy. It requires tremendous leadership skills. You’re one short hop from a mutiny or getting eaten or torn apart by the mob. [78] Money is good as a form of leverage. It means every time you make a decision, you multiply it with money. [1] Capital is a trickier form of leverage to use. It’s more modern. It’s the one that people have used to get fabulously wealthy in the last century. It’s probably been the dominant form of leverage in the last century. You can see this by looking for the richest people. It’s bankers, politicians in corrupt countries who print money, essentially people who move large amounts of money around. If you look at the top of very large companies, outside of technology companies, in many, many large old companies, the CEO job is really a financial job. It scales very, very well. If you get good at managing capital, you can manage more and more capital much more easily than you can manage more and more people. The final form of leverage is brand new—the most democratic form. It is: “products with no marginal cost of replication.” This includes books, media, movies, and code. Code is probably the most powerful form of permissionless leverage. All you need is a computer—you don’t need anyone’s permission.

title: Build or Buy Equity in a Business

content:
Ownership versus wage work. If you are paid for renting out your time, even lawyers and doctors, you can make some money, but you’re not going to make the money that gives you financial freedom. You’re not going to have passive income where a business is earning for you while you are on vacation.
Without ownership, your inputs are very closely tied to your outputs. In almost any salaried job, even one paying a lot per hour like a lawyer or a doctor, you’re still putting in the hours, and every hour you get paid.
Without ownership, when you’re sleeping, you’re not earning. When you’re retired, you’re not earning. When you’re on vacation, you’re not earning. And you can’t earn nonlinearly.
Essentially, you’re working for somebody else, and that person is taking on the risk and has the accountability, the intellectual property, and the brand. They’re not going to pay you enough. They’re going to pay you the bare minimum they have to, to get you to do their job. That can be a high bare minimum, but it’s still not going to be true wealth where you’re retired but still earning. [78] Owning equity in a company basically means you own the upside. When you own debt, you own guaranteed revenue streams and you own the downside. You want to own equity. If you don’t own equity in a business, your odds of making money are very slim. You have to work up to the point where you can own equity in a business. You could own equity as a small shareholder where you bought stock. You could also own it as an owner where you started the company. Ownership is really important.

Seek wealth, not money or status. Wealth is having assets that earn while you sleep. Money is how we transfer time and wealth. Status is your place in the social hierarchy.
Ignore people playing status games. They gain status by attacking people playing wealth creation games.
You’re not going to get rich renting out your time. You must own equity—a piece of a business—to gain your financial freedom.
You will get rich by giving society what it wants but does not yet know how to get. At scale.
Pick an industry where you can play long-term games with long-term people.
The internet has massively broadened the possible space of careers. Most people haven’t figured this out yet.
↓ Play iterated games. All the returns in life, whether in wealth, relationships, or knowledge, come from compound interest.
↓ Pick business partners with high intelligence, energy, and, above all, integrity.
↓ Don’t partner with cynics and pessimists. Their beliefs are self-fulfilling.
↓ Learn to sell. Learn to build. If you can do both, you will be unstoppable.

↓ Embrace accountability, and take business risks under your own name. Society will reward you with responsibility, equity, and leverage.
↓ “Give me a lever long enough and a place to stand, and I will move the earth.” —Archimedes
↓ Fortunes require leverage. Business leverage comes from capital, people, and products with no marginal cost of replication (code and media).
↓ Capital means money. To raise money, apply your specific knowledge with accountability and show resulting good judgment.
↓ Labor means people working for you. It’s the oldest and most fought-over form of leverage. Labor leverage will impress your parents, but don’t waste your life chasing it.
↓ Capital and labor are permissioned leverage. Everyone is chasing capital, but someone has to give it to you. Everyone is trying to lead, but someone has to follow you.
↓ Code and media are permissionless leverage. They’re the leverage behind the newly rich. You can create software and media that works for you while you sleep.
↓ An army of robots is freely available—it’s just packed in data centers for heat and space efficiency. Use it.
↓ If you can’t code, write books and blogs, record videos and podcasts.
↓ Leverage is a force multiplier for your judgment.
↓ Judgment requires experience but can be built faster by learning foundational skills.
↓ There is no skill called “business.” Avoid business magazines and business classes.
↓ Study microeconomics, game theory, psychology, persuasion, ethics, mathematics, and computers.
↓ Reading is faster than listening. Doing is faster than watching.
↓ You should be too busy to “do coffee” while still keeping an uncluttered calendar.
↓ Set and enforce an aspirational personal hourly rate. If fixing a problem will save less than your hourly rate, ignore it. If outsourcing a task will cost less than your hourly rate, outsource it.

↓ Become the best in the world at what you do. Keep redefining what you do until this is true.
↓ There are no get-rich-quick schemes. Those are just someone else getting rich off you.
↓ Apply specific knowledge, with leverage, and eventually you will get what you deserve.

content: I absolutely cannot let people think I am stingy. So, I frequently invite friends to restaurants; I also need a luxury car to display my status; furthermore, I must pay some other expenses—taxes. Finally, I have to turn to this great invention: the credit card. With a credit card, I don’t have to pay myself; the people at the credit card company will help me pay, at least temporarily… After that, I heard someone say, “He is truly a winner in life; he is living a first-class life.” I was living a first-class life: not drinking sparkling wine—only champagne; not eating a steak—only prime tenderloin. I wanted to live like a rich person in a futuristic world. And soon, the past began to constantly bother me in the form of bills, collection letters, and high loan interest rates. As a high-performing, high-income salesperson, I was always able to get a new credit card. So, I started making revolving payments, meaning I would get a new credit card and then use the new card to pay off the bill of the old credit card. Just like that, I spiraled into a downward financial state.

content:
Achieving financial security requires that the most important standard—the availability of money—is met. You must have a daily income. Therefore, it is best to put your money in a safe or invest it in a cash fund. You should not take risks until you achieve financial security. Consequently, you should choose low-risk investment projects. However, even so, you must pay attention to managing potential risks. Never put all your money into a single investment project, even if “all your funds” only total 1,000 Euros. Remember, managing risk means increasing the opportunity for profit. Before achieving financial security, keep financial safety at the center. You should tolerate a low profit rate and keep some cash in a bank savings account. If you still want to invest, I recommend a deposit plan.
The 40:40:20 Principle Guarantees Financial Security To achieve financial security, you must change the allocation ratio of your money. Although most of the money must still be put into low-risk investments, you can allocate 40% to moderately risky investments. If you consistently hold this money without using it, the risk will be greatly reduced through the effect of “average cost return.” The remaining 20% can be invested in high-risk projects, which involves speculative funds such as emerging market funds or national funds, as well as all special funds and corporate participation funds. The risk of these funds can also be reduced over time through the effect of “average cost return.” On the other hand, your probability of profit is also extremely high. One important point is: you absolutely cannot put the money used to guarantee your financial security into high-risk or speculative projects. You must not touch this money. The investments you make must guarantee that your financial security is never affected.
summary: Achieving financial security requires that the most important standard—the availability of money—is met. You must have a daily income. Therefore, it is best to put your money in a safe or invest it in a cash fund. You should not take risks until you achieve financial security. Consequently, you should choose low-risk investment projects. However, even so, you must pay attention to managing potential risks. Never put all your money into a single investment project, even if “all your funds” only total 1,000 Euros. Remember, managing risk means increasing the opportunity for profit. content:
The Foundation of Wealth Building Financial freedom is a goal that anyone today can achieve, of course, this requires us to have the courage to pursue the life we truly desire. As a famous saying goes: “It is not the difficulty that makes us give up, but rather that we give up, which makes it seem so difficult.”
If we keep the laws of money in mind, we will find that our financial situation is steadily improving. Nothing can stop a mindset that aligns with the times. This also applies to everyone’s life. Nothing can stop us from enjoying the right we are born with—wealth. A life of dignity and financial comfort aligns with our natural laws. As long as we don’t give up, nothing can prevent us from reaching this goal.
Making a Dream Album To achieve financial freedom, we must have motivation. Therefore, the first thing we must do is think up 10 reasons (wishes) why we want to become wealthy, and write them down. This will be the driving force for our actions.
Next, from these 10 reasons for wanting to become wealthy, select the top 3 most important ones. Don’t set yourself too many goals, as that might be unrealistic. Human desires are endless, and we need to distinguish between primary and secondary, determining which are the most important goals. After setting the goals, we must find ways to achieve them.
One method taught by Qianqian to Jia is to use a Dream Album and a Dream Piggy Bank: the Dream Album is used to collect photos related to your wishes, and you paste them into the album.
Looking at the Album Daily The act of thinking through pictures and imagining the scenarios where you achieve your wishes is called “visualization.”
Preparing a Dream Piggy Bank Prepare a piggy bank for each dream, and write your dream on it. Once the piggy bank is ready, save every penny you save into it.
When Jia doubted whether the Dream Album would be effective, Qianqian said: “Curiosity is good, but it must never hinder your actions. Too many people hesitate in their actions simply because they feel they haven’t fully understood the matter. Putting it into practice is much more useful than pure thinking.”
When we question whether this fantasy is a “pipe dream,” we need to know that “successful people are successful because they always dream of the day they succeed, constantly imagining the situation when they have achieved their dreams. Of course, people cannot remain stuck in dreams.”
“Learning is the process of recognizing new concepts and new ideas. If people always consider problems using the same way of thinking, they will always get the same results. Don’t jump to conclusions before you have done it.”
People without imagination find it difficult to achieve great things. The more effort we put into something, the greater the possibility of success. But most people put their energy into things they don’t like, instead of imagining what they hope to gain.
Don’t approach it with a “let’s try” mindset; take concrete action! If you only approach it with a “let’s try” mindset, it will only end in failure, and we will achieve nothing. ‘Trying’ is merely an excuse; before we even try, we have already prepared an escape route for ourselves. There is no option to ’try’; there are only two choices—to do it or not to do it."
Success Journal When we do something, we need sufficient self-confidence. Our level of confidence determines whether we believe in our ability and whether we believe in ourselves. If we fundamentally don’t believe we can do it, we won’t even start, and if we don’t start, we will gain nothing."
Therefore, we need to keep a “Success Journal.” The “Success Journal” is similar to a diary; record all the things you have successfully done in it, writing down at least 5 personal achievements every day, no matter how small. The main purpose of doing this is to help us boost our self-confidence.
At the beginning, we might feel it’s difficult, and we might ask ourselves, “Can this or that thing really be counted as an achievement?” In this case, our answer should be affirmative. Being overly confident is much better than being insufficiently confident."
When we encounter problems:
a. Still stick to your idea Everyone can do this when things are normal. It is only when true difficulties arise that the difference becomes clear. Only a few people can firmly implement their plans. Very successful people even have the ability to perform exceptionally when things are at their most difficult.
b. When progress is smooth Even when everything is progressing very smoothly, you must firmly stick to your plan.
c. The 72-Hour Rule When we decide to do something, we must complete it within 72 hours, otherwise, we are likely to never do it again."
“How much money a person earns is linked to their self-confidence. Furthermore, whether their experiences are focused within their scope of ability or placed outside of what they can achieve is also very important. Without a Success Journal, we won’t think about in which areas we are suited to earn money.”
Often, our inability to act stems from the psychology of fear. Fear always appears when we imagine how things might go wrong. The more we think about the possibility of failure, the more afraid we become. But when we look at our Success Journal, we notice the successful things, and naturally, we think about how to do them."
Earning and Saving Money When Qianqian encouraged Jia to bravely earn money, she told the story of a young boy named Darryl. Darryl became a millionaire at the age of 17 through personal effort, making him a role model for Jia.
In Darryl’s story, a businessman gave Darryl (Jia’s role model) advice on earning money:
Figure out what you like, and then figure out how to earn money from it. Solve a problem for others, and you will earn a lot of money; Focus your energy on what you know, what you can do, and what you possess. Before buying something, ask yourself, “Is this really necessary?” Mr. Jin, when guiding Jia not to spend all the money she had immediately, told the story of a goose that lays golden eggs:
A goose raised by a farmer lays a golden egg every day. The farmer was very greedy and hoped the goose would lay at least two golden eggs every day. In a fit of pique, he killed the goose, and from then on, he never received another golden egg. The goose is the principal, and the golden egg is the interest. The farmer’s biggest mistake was not “killing” his “goose.”
Expenditure and income are directly proportional; the higher the income, the higher the expenditure, unless you learn to allocate your assets reasonably and learn to spend within your means.
Advice for Those in Debt: a. Destroy all credit cards Spending with a credit card costs more than spending with cash.
b. Pay the minimum installment amount within the allowed limit The higher the installment amount, the less living money you have left each month. Often, people underestimate how high their living expenses are, and they might take out new loans to pay off old ones when a large expense occurs.
c. For consumer loans For loans for goods in daily life, such as a TV loan, it is best not to apply for it first. If you do apply, save half of the money remaining after deducting living expenses, and use the other half to pay the consumer loan.
Fund Allocation The author suggests that we can divide our income into Daily Expenses (10%) + Dream Goals (40%) + Golden Goose Account (50%). This means we can save 50% of our income, and this money should not be easily touched; it is like the goose mentioned earlier that lays golden eggs, allowing money to generate more money.
Of the remaining 50%, besides the 10% needed for daily life, the remaining 40% is saved to achieve the dreams we want, such as buying a phone as a reward for yourself, or going on a trip, etc. This amount is up to you to manage and plan; remember to allocate it reasonably.
Golden Goose: From the story of laying golden eggs, the “goose” refers to the money (savings value), and the “golden egg” refers to the interest.
Never kill your goose, and don’t use all your money to pay off loans, leaving yourself with nothing. Having nothing is not our goal; our goal is to achieve the initial 3 wishes or accumulate the savings.
Passive Income Investment Tips:
Invest money in a safe place. Money should lay many “golden eggs” (choose high interest, with the highest dividends coming from stocks). Investment should be simple and clear, easy to operate. The 72 Rule:
Divide 72 by the annual profit percentage of the investment, and the resulting number is the number of years required for that money to double.
Divide 72 by a certain inflation rate, and you can find out how many years it will take for the money to lose half its value.
When the market declines, losses only occur when you actually sell the fund.
A fund has an indicator—the Fluctuation Rate (Volatility): a lower fluctuation rate means higher safety and more stable profit growth. Funds generally last 5 to 10 years; the market always has ups and downs, but the overall trend is upward, so you can check the market after 5 or 10 years.
72 / Return Rate = Time to Double 72 / Inflation Rate = Time to Half Value 115 Rule: 115 / Return Rate = Time to Double
Controlling Risk Cash Reserves are Necessary You cannot put all your money into stocks or funds; you must reserve some cash to have liquid funds, so that when the stock market declines, you can buy appropriately at the right time. The remaining reserve cash can be invested in short-term income projects, such as daily deposits. Bank passbooks are merely money-swallowing machines; their returns are often less than the losses caused by inflation. Some savings accounts have high interest rates, but they require keeping the cash in the bank for a relatively long time, so the author does not recommend relying solely on bank passbooks.
Qianqian’s Words Some people who read this book do not absorb what you say, and thus make no changes. Others, after reading it, begin to manage their finances wisely, and they will lead happier and wealthier lives.

summary:
Mr. Willy’s desk is always a mess because he is incompetent. A messy desk indicates a confused mind, which can only mean one thing: he is unfit for his job.

The statement above is actually very simple: “He is incompetent, so his desk is messy; because his desk is messy, he is unable to perform his job.”

Fallacies (or Logical Errors)

1. Appeal to Ignorance (or Argument from Ignorance) When we conclude that something is true simply because it “has not been proven false,” or conclude that it is false simply because it “has not been proven true,” our judgment contains a logical flaw. For example, although no one has found evidence of Atlantis’s existence yet, this does not mean that Atlantis does not exist.
title: A logical flaw caused by poor arguments (or weak premises)

summary:
· Either/Or (Dichotomy) Just because there are only two choices presented, one cannot assume that one of them is necessarily correct. Many things are not strictly “either/or” or “black/white.” For example: “Since you don’t support free trade, you must support protectionism!”

· Middle Value (Moderation) Many people prefer to take the middle ground between two choices because it avoids either extreme. This practice is sometimes referred to as the Doctrine of the Mean (or Golden Mean). “The junior high teacher believes that the school should arrange a fixed curriculum schedule. Meanwhile, the parents believe that students should be able to choose their courses freely. Therefore, the best solution is to combine the two.”
title: Logical flaw resulting from incorrect assumptions

content:
· Error of Asserting the Conclusion We cannot conclude that “when B is true, A is true” just because “when A is true, B is true.” This error is also called the “Conversion Error.” “Every time I go on vacation, I feel very relaxed. Therefore, when I feel very relaxed, I must be on vacation.” Relaxation during vacation does not mean that relaxation only happens during vacation; I might relax at home, I might relax while eating dinner, I might feel relaxed while chatting with friends… Therefore, the fallacy of the statement above is obvious.
· Negation of the Antecedent We cannot conclude that “if A is not true, B is not true” just because “if A is true, B is true.” “Every time it rains, the ground gets wet. Last night it didn’t rain, so the ground cannot be wet.” Without a doubt, many situations can make the ground wet; it doesn’t necessarily have to rain.

content:
Distorting Viewpoint
Literal Translation: Straw Man Other Names: Straw Dummy / Misrepresentation
It is the act of distorting an opponent’s arguments to make them easier to attack.
By exaggerating, twisting, or even completely fabricating an opponent’s arguments, one presents their own position as more reasonable. However, sincere and rational debate is destroyed by this form of argumentation, which is essentially fraud.
Example: Xiao Ming says: “The state should invest more funds in the medical and education sectors.” Xiao Liang replies: “That’s terrifying! You actually hate the country so much, that you want to reduce defense spending, leaving our army defenseless and unable to protect the nation.”
Note: The original English term for this fallacy, “strawman,” literally translates to “straw dummy.” Since a straw dummy is not a real person, it won’t offer any resistance in a fight, and it is very easy to knock down. In the UK, this fallacy is also often called “Aunt Sally.”
Causal Attribution Error
It is concluding that a causal relationship exists between two things, either genuinely existing or hypothetically assumed, based on the association between them.
It is assuming that a causal relationship exists between two things simply because they are associated, or merely because they exist simultaneously. Different things may occur simultaneously or sequentially, but this does not necessarily mean that one is the cause of the other. Sometimes, the association between two things is purely coincidental, and it is even possible that both things share the same cause.
Example: Xiao Ming points to a table and says, “Over the past few centuries, global temperatures have been rising, and at the same time, the number of pirates has been decreasing. Therefore, we can conclude: the existence of pirates lowers global temperatures, and global warming is a hoax.”
Emotional Blackmail (or Emotional Manipulation)
It is substituting genuine, effective arguments with the manipulation of emotions.
Emotional blackmail includes manipulating fear, jealousy, hatred, pity, pride, and so on. There is one very important thing we must know: sometimes a logically sound argument may trigger a strong emotional response. But abandoning logic and relying solely on appeals to emotion to mask the fact that one’s own viewpoint lacks strong evidence will only lead to more problems and fallacies. Every mentally healthy person is influenced by emotions, so emotional blackmail is a very common and effective debate strategy, but fundamentally, it is a flawed and hypocritical way of arguing, and it tends to rationalize the emotional state of the other party in the debate.
Example: Xiao Liang dislikes drinking mutton soup, but his father tells him, “Think about the children in poor African countries who are starving to death, those pitiful kids who can’t eat anything.”
Fallacy Leading to Error (or Fallacious Conclusion)
Literal Translation: Fallacy Fallacy Other Names: Mistaking Error for Error / Assuming Error
It is judging that a conclusion must be wrong simply because the level of argumentation is poor, or because the argument contains errors.
It is not logically sound to assume that a viewpoint must lead to a fallacious conclusion; even incorrect premises can be presented using sound logic. Similarly, it is entirely possible to prove a correct viewpoint using flawed premises in a debate, or to include logical fallacies in the process of argumentation.
Example: Xiao Li discovers that Xiao Hong advocates for a healthy diet merely because some dubious nutritionist claims, “A healthy diet is a popular lifestyle,” which is unreliable. But Xiao Li then concludes, “Therefore, the conclusion that a healthy diet is necessary is wrong, and binge eating every day is fine,” which is also a fallacy.
Slippery Slope
If A happens, then eventually bad thing Z will happen, so we cannot allow A to happen.
The problem is that this form of reasoning avoids discussing the current issue A, instead shifting the focus to the hypothetical extreme assumption Z. Furthermore, there is no evidence to prove that Z will necessarily happen because of A. This fallacy is also a form of emotional blackmail, using fear to undermine the fairness of the current discussion with unverified speculation.
Example: Xiao Qiang asserts that if we allow same-sex marriage, the next thing that will happen is that we will allow incestuous marriage, and even allow humans to marry monkeys or humans to marry cars.
Ad Hominem (Attacking the Person)
It is diminishing an opponent’s argument by attacking their personal character or other personal traits, such as height, appearance, social status, etc.
Ad hominem can be a public, blatant attack, or it can be a subtle implication that the opponent’s character is questionable, thereby discrediting their argument. In an argument, ad hominem often achieves the effect of defeating the opponent without a fight.
Example: Huihui presents undeniable evidence showing that the new tax system is fairer, more reasonable, and worth promoting. Zhuang asks the attendees: “Do you think you should believe anything said by a woman who is unmarried, has a criminal record, and smells like body odor?”
Tu Quoque (You Too)
Responding to criticism by criticizing the critic: To avoid directly addressing the criticism, one turns the accusation back onto the person who raised the criticism.
The original Latin term for this fallacy is tu quoque, meaning “you too (have done it).” This logical fallacy is commonly known as “hypocrisy of the critic.” It is usually a diversionary tactic that allows the party who must defend their argument to shift the focus from themselves back onto the person who raised the criticism.
Example: At the hospital, Xiao Mei points out that Xiao Li’s poor health condition is due to her failure to strictly follow the doctor’s orders. Instead of reflecting on why she didn’t follow the orders, Xiao Li blames Xiao Mei: “Don’t talk about me! You never listened to the doctor’s advice either; you never took your medicine on time!”
Note: In China, this fallacy is also known as the “Flea Theory” (臭虫论): Lu Xun, in his 1933 article “Foreigners Also Have,” satirized how Chinese people, when criticized, would claim that other countries also have the same errors to cover up their own mistakes. “All of China has it; foreign countries have it too. Foreigners say China has fleas, but the West also has fleas.”
Personal Limitation
Literal Translation: Self-Doubt
Due to one’s own level of understanding, one is unable or finds it difficult to comprehend something, and thus concludes that the matter might be wrong or false.
For discussions on certain complex topics, such as “biological evolution and natural selection,” one needs a basic knowledge base on the subject. Simply because one does not know this knowledge, one assumes that these theories must be wrong—this is a fallacy.
Example: Xiao Ming draws a fish and a human, and dismissively asks Xiao Qiang: “Look at these two creatures. Do you really think I would be stupid enough to believe that a fish can randomly transform into a human over time?”
Selective Exception (or Cherry Picking)
When a certain viewpoint is proven to be wrong, one changes the rules of discussion or uses a special exception to excuse the error.
Foolish humans are always reluctant to admit they are wrong. They are not only unwilling to improve their understanding of the problem through better comprehension, but sometimes they stubbornly try to find ways to prove their own correctness. The common method is to find a rationalizing reason for their error after the fact. It is easy to find a reason to believe in what we are accustomed to, but the real difficulty lies in how we test our own worldview after others have confirmed our error, and how we correct our thoughts.
Example: Xiao Ming claims he can predict the future. When everyone tests his predictions in a reasonable scientific environment, he retreats. Xiao Ming says you must first believe that he has precognitive ability before you can see his predictions come true.
Presupposition Questioning (or Leading Question)
Also called “Inductive Questioning,” this involves pre-inserting an assumption into a question, making it so that the respondent, no matter how they answer, appears to be in the wrong.
Presupposition questioning is particularly effective in undermining rational debate because it is provocative. The respondent is often forced to panic and defend themselves.
For example: Xiao Mei and Xiao Li both like Ah Hui. One time, while Ah Hui was present, Xiao Mei deliberately asked Xiao Li in a curious tone: “Xiao Li, have you stopped gambling now?” (The question presupposes that Xiao Li used to gamble.)
Burden of Proof
Assuming that the responsibility of providing evidence lies not with the person proposing the view, but with the person questioning the view.
The person who makes the claim must provide the evidence; the responsibility should not be thrown onto the person who doubts the argument. Just because a view cannot be falsified or no counterexample can be presented does not automatically prove that the view is reasonable or credible. At the same time, we must clearly understand that “nothing is absolute,” so we need to strengthen the credibility of the argument based on known evidence. Dismissing a view simply because it hasn’t been proven is also a fallacy of inference.
Example: Xiao Qiang says he can see ghosts. Just because other people cannot see ghosts does not prove whether his statement is true or not.
Double Entendre
Using a statement with a double meaning or an ambiguous statement that contains ambiguity to mislead or distort the facts.
Politicians often utilize ambiguous statements, and when they are exposed, they point out that, theoretically, what they said was not entirely a lie. But in essence, these statements are misleading from the very beginning.
Example: Zhuang asks A Cong: “You always say you’ll treat me to a meal. When can you fulfill that promise?” A Cong replies: “I’ll go buy you a packet of instant noodles in a bit.”
Gambler’s Fallacy
Believing that there are predictable patterns in independent, random events.
It is like the winning rate of a roulette wheel. Generally speaking, the probability of a single repeated result occurring is extremely low, and the location of the ball each time is completely unrelated to the previous time. For instance, although there is a tiny possibility of twenty consecutive coin flips all landing on heads, the probability of each individual flip landing on heads is still 50/50, and this probability is not affected by the previous flips.
Example: When rolling dice, six consecutive “Big” numbers appear. Zhuang believes that the next roll must definitely be “Small.” As a result, he loses everything.
Blind Conformity (or Bandwagon Effect)
Literal Translation: Bandwagon
Believing that something is correct simply because many people are doing it or agreeing with it.
The fallacy of this viewpoint lies in the fact that the popularity or acceptance of something is completely unrelated to whether it is right or wrong. If we decide right or wrong based on public acceptance, then in the era when people believed the Earth was flat, the Earth should have been flat.
Example: Drunken Old Wang points to Old Zhang and says: “If monsters are just foolish superstitions, why do so many people still believe they truly exist?”
Note: The original English term for this fallacy, “bandwagon,” generally refers to the magnificent carriage carrying a band in a circus parade, and the derived meaning is “a trend or fashion accepted by the public.”
Appeal to Authority
The belief that what an authority figure says must be correct.
It is important to remember that this fallacy does not mean that the claims of a reasonable expert or scientific consensus are unimportant; rather, it means that appealing to authority is not a valid form of argumentation, and the authority’s opinion can also be completely wrong. Therefore, whether someone is an authority or not has no essential impact on whether their claim is true. However, unless a person has a level of understanding or empirical evidence similar to that of an expert, it is unreasonable to disregard the statement of someone with deep knowledge.
Example: Old Zhang doesn’t know how to defend his position that evolution “is not real,” so he says: “I know a famous scientist, Zhuang Zhuang, who also questions evolution!” In fact, Zhuang Zhuang is just a successful fitness coach.
Hasty Generalization
Literal Translation: Combination Division (or Part-to-Whole)
Assuming that a local characteristic of something is the overall characteristic of that thing, or that it applies to other parts of that thing; or that the overall characteristic of an object must apply to each of its independent parts.
This fallacy is also called the “Fallacy of Composition/Division.” Usually, when something is correct for a part, it is indeed possible that it applies to the whole, and vice versa—like saying, “Peeking through a tube, one can see a glimpse.” But the key point is whether there is effective evidence to show that the situation is indeed like that. Simply observing certain consistencies in something may lead to biased thinking, causing us to assume that the consistency exists where it actually does not.
Example: Xiao Cong is a precocious child with logical thinking. He knows that atoms, which are invisible to the naked eye, make up him, so he concludes that he cannot be seen. Unfortunately, despite his thoughts, he still lost the game of hide-and-seek.
Purifying the Argument (or Moving the Goalposts)
Literal Translation: Not a True Scotsman
It is the act of adding premises after the fact, constantly modifying or “purifying” the argument, to refute criticism of your argument’s flaws.
In this form of faulty reasoning, no matter how convincing the evidence is for someone’s belief, simply by changing the standard, the evidence can be made inapplicable to the fabricated so-called “true” example. This post-hoc rationalization is a way of avoiding reasonable criticism of one’s own argument.
Example: A Liang says that Cantonese people only eat sweet tofu pudding. A Hui says that he is Cantonese, but he eats savory tofu pudding. A Liang gets particularly angry and tells A Hui: “True Cantonese people only eat sweet tofu pudding!”
Note: The original English term for this fallacy is “no true Scotsman,” meaning “not a true Scotsman.” It comes from the work On Thinking by Professor Anthony Flew, published in 1975, where he cited a Scotsman who, in order to deny that Scotsmen commit serious crimes, said, “No true Scotsman would do such a thing.”
Genetic Determinism (or Origin Determinism)
Literal Translation: Gene Determines
Judging the good or bad, right or wrong of something based on its origin or the person who proposed the viewpoint.
Also called genetic determinism: Good people and bad people are predetermined in their genes, such as, “You are inherently a bad person, so you are destined only to do bad things and never do good things.” It attempts to evade positive debate by focusing on the origin of a person or thing. Similar to the “Ad Hominem” fallacy, it attacks and discredits the opponent’s viewpoint by utilizing known negative perceptions, yet it doesn’t actually explain what is wrong with the opponent’s argument.
Example: A news channel plays a seismic alert message. Xiao Liang comforts Xiao Hong, saying, “We all know that the news channel, besides celebrity gossip, never broadcasts serious news.”
False Dichotomy (or Black or White)
Only offering two options as choices, while completely ignoring the existence of other possibilities.
Also called “either/or,” “dilemma reasoning,” or “false reasoning.” This insidious strategy superficially presents a logical argument, but upon closer inspection, one can find that there are many more possibilities than the binary choices presented. The binary, black-or-white mindset does not allow for the existence of various variables, conditions, and contexts beyond two possibilities. It only misleads the argument and blocks rational, honest debate.
Example: The Supreme Commander says: “Anyone who doesn’t support his grand blueprint of ‘Making America Great Again’ is an enemy of America.”
Circular Reasoning
The premise of the argument already contains the conclusion.
Such self-contained logic is usually rooted in deep-seated, obsessive assumptions. For example, the cliché: “The main reason circular reasoning is bad is because it is bad.”
Example: The Bullshit Journal is flawless. We know this because The Bullshit Journal itself once stated: “Everything in The Bullshit Journal is true and beautiful; you must not have any doubts.”
Appeal to Nature
Simply because something is “natural” or “of nature,” one assumes it is perfect, and its rationality and effectiveness are indisputable.
Many naturally occurring things are considered beneficial, which may cause our cognition to become biased. Nature itself does not make things good or bad. For example, killing in nature can be seen as very “natural,” but this does not mean that killing is beneficial or rational.
Example: Zhuang believes in “natural remedies,” so when he has a cold or fever, he only drinks plain boiled water, and when he is sick, he only eats herbs. Because he believes that plain boiled water or herbs are more natural than chemically synthesized drugs, they must be more beneficial.
Anecdotal Evidence (or Hearsay)
Using personal experience or isolated cases to replace irrefutable evidence or sound arguments.
People are usually more inclined to believe the statements of others than to understand complex data and changes as a whole. Quantitative scientific measurement is almost always more accurate than personal perception and experience, but we tend to believe things that are tangibly present to us, and what people we trust say, rather than the reality shown by what looks more “abstract” statistics.
Example: Xiao Jie’s grandfather smokes 30 cigarettes a day and still lives to 97 years old. Therefore, Xiao Jie concludes that the research findings proving a causal relationship between smoking and lung cancer cannot be trusted.
Causal Displacement (or Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc)
Literal Translation: Texas Sharpshooter
Only selecting evidence that favors oneself or matches one’s own hypothesis.
Although shooting first and then drawing a target center on the bullet hole makes the shooter look like a sharpshooter, there is no necessary causal relationship between the bullet hitting the bullseye and the shooter being a sharpshooter.
Example: Coca-Cola claims that research shows that in the five countries where Coca-Cola sells the most, three countries are among the top ten globally for average IQ. Therefore, drinking Coca-Cola can improve IQ.
Note: The original English term for this fallacy is “the Texas sharpshooter,” referring to a Texas shooter who shoots first and then draws a target.
Middle Ground (or Compromise)
The compromise, or middle ground, between two extremes must certainly be the location of the truth.
Often, the truth does lie between two extreme points, but this can also cause us to develop a cognitive bias: sometimes something is fundamentally wrong, even if it is a compromise. The middle ground between truth and fallacy is still a fallacy.
Example: Xiao Li firmly believes that vaccination causes autism in children, but A Cong, her friend who likes research, says that this claim has been scientifically proven to be false. Then their friend Xiao Mei proposes a compromise argument: Vaccination inevitably causes certain types of autism, not all types of autism.

Distorting Viewpoint

Literal Translation: Straw Man Other Names: Straw Dummy / Misrepresentation

It is the act of distorting an opponent’s arguments to make them easier to attack.

By exaggerating, twisting, or even completely fabricating an opponent’s arguments, one presents their own position as more reasonable. However, sincere and rational debate is destroyed by this form of argumentation, which is essentially fraud.

Example: Xiao Ming says: “The state should invest more funds in the medical and education sectors.” Xiao Liang replies: “That’s terrifying! You actually hate the country so much, that you want to reduce defense spending, leaving our army defenseless and unable to protect the nation.”
title: The 24 Common Logical Fallacies

content:
People who fall into traps usually have two motivations:
One is the economic motivation, which is a rational motivation—the desire to minimize financial losses. The other is the non-economic motivation: the desire to regain face and punish the opponent.
There are many such traps in life:
For example, two deputy directors want to be promoted and compete by giving gifts. The gifts already given are sunk costs, which cannot be recovered unless you, as the deputy director, decide you don’t want to do it anymore. Another example is the game Zheng Tu (征途): This is a game that changed the landscape of online gaming. In an era where everything required clicking a card, it was permanently free to operate. When you try it for free for a while, you are quickly drawn into the game world. However, you gradually realize that if you don’t pay, you aren’t really playing the game—you are being played by the game. Those “RMB players” who possess various luxurious equipment and high levels will crush you to the point of misery, making you feel your self-esteem has been completely trampled. So, you angrily shout, “Isn’t it because of the RMB? I have it too!” and immediately purchase the full set of luxurious equipment, instantly leveling up, thereby completely defeating the previous defeat and achieving a triumphant return.
But is that all? Of course not. You feel satisfied, so the person who defeated you feels unsatisfied, and thus, you both fall into the trap.
By making people crave the recovery of face, they encourage infinite spending (or “氪金” - kè jīn, i.e., paying to spend/grind) to win back that face. Ultimately, this achieves the goal of sending money to the company.

content:
We need to understand the difference between earning returns on equity and receiving salary compensation. If you are compensated by renting out your time, even if you work in high-paying professions like law or medicine, the compensation you receive will be very limited, insufficient to allow you to achieve financial freedom. However, if you own corporate shares, you can receive passive income—meaning the company continues to make money for you even when you are on vacation.
Fundamentally, working a job means working for someone else. Meanwhile, corporate owners possess intellectual property and brand value while also bearing the risk and responsibility. Therefore, the compensation they pay you is always less than the value you create. To get you to work, they will provide you with the minimum necessary compensation.

content:
The first type is labor leverage, which means having others work for you. Labor leverage is one of the oldest forms of leverage, but in modern society, its effectiveness is not the best. [1] I even think it is the most outdated form of leverage. This is because managing other people is a very complex and challenging job that requires superb leadership skills. If done poorly, the manager might end up ostracized and devoured by their subordinates.
Capital is the second, relatively better form of leverage. Capital leverage means using money to expand the influence of decisions. [1] Capital is a more modern form of leverage, and utilizing capital leverage is somewhat difficult, requiring a certain skill set. In the 20th century, people achieved astonishing wealth by utilizing capital leverage. Capital leverage was the primary form of leverage in the 20th century. If you look at the wealthiest people, you will find that the richest are bankers and politicians in corrupt countries—they are essentially all people who can mobilize large amounts of capital. Look at the executives of large companies; besides tech companies, the CEOs of most established large companies are actually doing financial work. The amplifying effect of capital leverage is very obvious. Managing capital is easier than managing people because as capital continuously grows, the difficulty of managing it is far lower than managing an ever-expanding team.
The last type of leverage is the newest and the most accessible to ordinary people. This leverage is “products with zero marginal cost of reproduction.” This includes books, media, movies, and code. Among all leverages that can be used without needing permission from others, code is arguably the most powerful—it only requires a computer.

content:
1. People Should Seek Wealth, Not Money or Status People should not earn wealth through arduous work. Working 80 hours a week in a restaurant will not make you richer. Hard work is unavoidable, but it should be done in the right way. People should seek wealth, not money or status. If you believe wealth is unimportant, wealth will move away from you. Wealth is assets that continue to make money while you sleep. Without wealth-generating assets, when you sleep, you have no income; when you retire, you cannot keep earning money. In short, without wealth, you cannot achieve non-linear earning. Generally, wealth is created by starting your own company or by investing. Neither of these is achieved by putting in a massive amount of time; the ultra-rich, just like you, only have 24 hours every day.
2. The Key to Acquiring Wealth To acquire wealth, you can provide something valuable to the masses—especially something they don’t know how to obtain. And you must supply it on a large scale. The internet has greatly expanded career possibilities, and most people still lack a clear understanding of this. Learn marketing, learn creation. If you master these two things, nothing can stop you from succeeding.
3. Arm Yourself with Special Knowledge Special knowledge is knowledge that cannot be acquired through training. If it can be acquired through training, others can also acquire it, and they can replace you. Special knowledge is usually high in technical sophistication and creative. It cannot be outsourced or automated. (For example, insight) It can be discovered when driven by genuine curiosity and passion. The process of creating special knowledge feels like playing to you, but like working to others. Usually, special knowledge lies at the boundaries of knowledge—things that are either newly understood or genuinely difficult to understand. If you do not commit 100%, someone who commits 100% will surpass you. And they won’t just be slightly better; they will be much better, because in the realm of ideas, compound interest will work, and leverage will work. Special knowledge might be things like: Sales skills. Having musical talent. Persistence: This means you can research things with dedication. Loving science fiction: This means you can quickly absorb a lot of knowledge. Playing many games: This means you have a good understanding of game theory. Gossip: This might help you become a very interesting journalist. Special knowledge is a strange combination, coming from your DNA, your unique environment of growth, and your response to that knowledge. These are almost integrated into your personality and identity, and then you can continuously refine them. Study microeconomics, game theory, psychology, brainwashing techniques, ethics, mathematics, and computer science.
4. Arm Yourself with Leverage Business leverage mainly consists of capital, labor, and products with extremely low replication costs (code and media). Capital refers to money. To raise funds, you need to use your special knowledge, combined with your sense of responsibility, to demonstrate your good judgment. Labor refers to the people who work for you. It is the oldest and most fiercely contested form of leverage. Labor leverage will make your parents feel proud, but don’t waste your life pursuing this alone. Capital and labor are forms of leverage that require permission to use. Everyone chases capital, but there must always be someone to pay for it. Everyone wants to lead others, but there must always be subordinates. Code and media are forms of leverage that require no permission; they are the leverage behind the new rich. You can create software and media that work for you even while you sleep. A large group of robots is available for free use—to save space and energy efficiency, they are packaged into data centers; use them! By applying special knowledge combined with leverage, you will ultimately get what you deserve.
5. In One Sentence: Productize Yourself What does this mean? “Productize” and “yourself.” “Yourself” has uniqueness; “productize” has leverage. “Am I productizing it? Can I scale it? Can I amplify it through labor, capital, code, or media?” So, this phrase is very easy to remember. If you want to be richer, you must figure out what you can provide to society that society doesn’t know how to obtain, but that society wants, and providing it to you is natural and within your skill set and capability. Next, you must find a way to scale it, because producing only one is far from enough. You might need to produce thousands, or tens of thousands, or millions, or even billions, so that everyone can have one. Steve Jobs (and his team, of course) figured out that society needed a smartphone. This smartphone had all the functions of phones at the time, but also many other new functions, and it was easier to use. Therefore, they figured out how to manufacture the smartphone, and then they figured out how to mass-produce the smartphone. You must become the person who can scale the provision of these products or services. This is the real challenge of how to make money.
6. Pay Attention to Your Character In my life, I have known some extremely successful, very popular, and very smart people. However, I have seen them do one or two things that were not very good for others. I would say, “Hey, I think you shouldn’t do this to others. Because it will ultimately hurt yourself.” Deep down, we all know who we are. You cannot hide anything from yourself. You are very clear whether what you do is right or wrong; if you have too many moral flaws, you will not respect yourself. The worst outcome in this world is a lack of self-respect. If you don’t love yourself, who will love you? If I see someone doing this, the first time I will remind them, but usually they won’t change, and then I will keep my distance from them. I cut them out of my life. If someone constantly claims to be honest, they are likely dishonest. These are just some effective indicators that I have learned. When someone spends a lot of time talking about their values or talking about themselves, it means they are hiding something. I think to myself: “If you want to get close to me, your values must be better than mine.”
7. Smart People Truly Understand One Thing If someone uses many complex words and many grand concepts, they are likely unaware of what they are actually talking about. I believe the smartest people can explain things to a child. If you cannot explain it to a child, then you don’t truly know it. Truly smart thinkers are clear-thinking thinkers; they understand very, very basic foundational knowledge.
8. Step Outside Yourself to See the Truth Imagine one of my friends is going through some difficulties, such as a breakup, career issues, business failure, or health problems. When he needs my advice, it often takes me only a few minutes to accurately tell him, “Oh, that girl, forget her. Anyway, she’s not good for you. You will be happier. Believe me. You will find someone more suitable in the future.” But he himself finds it difficult to see this. Because he is in pain and torment, his desires conflict with reality, which prevents him from seeing the truth clearly. The same thing happens when we make decisions. To see the truth clearly, you must set aside the self, because the self does not want to face the truth.
9. What is Truly Important is Leisure Time Great ideas only come after you feel bored. Good ideas never appear when you are under pressure, busy, rushing around, or in a hurry. If your schedule doesn’t have one or two days a week where you aren’t constantly in meetings or constantly busy, you cannot think. You won’t have good ideas related to your business. You also cannot make good judgments. I encourage you to set aside at least one day a week (better yet, two days, because if you prepare two days, you will definitely find one) so that you have time to think. Cherish your time; it is everything. It is more important than your money. It is more important than your friends. It is more important than anything. Your time is everything. Don’t waste your time.
10. Reading Can Make You Successful Spending one hour a day reading science, mathematics, and philosophy can likely put you on the high ladder of human success within seven years. I have spent a lot of time reading. My only true friend is books. Books are great friends because they tell you the wisdom of the best thinkers over the past thousands of years. Any book that has survived for two thousand years has been screened by many people, and it is more likely to be correct; I want to reread these books. The fact is, I read not for self-improvement. I read out of curiosity and interest. The best book is the one that captivates you.
11. Do Things for Your Own Goals I truly want to do things for my own goals. Whether it is business, fitness, romance, friendship, or anything else, I believe the meaning of life is to do things for your own goals. When you do things for yourself, you can create your best work. Even if you do these things to make money, you will actually be the most successful. Follow your true curiosity, not the current hot topics. If your curiosity leads you to where society will eventually go, you will receive rich rewards. When you are dating, there is a moment you realize that the relationship will not lead to marriage, you might be better off moving on. When you are learning something, such as geography or history, and you realize you will never use this information, drop that course. That is wasting time. That is wasting mental energy.
12. Become a Better Decision-Maker Overall Become a better decision-maker overall. Decision-making is everything. Yes. Decision-making is everything. In fact, someone who makes correct decisions 80% of the time instead of 70% of the time will have value and compensation in the market hundreds of times higher. I believe people find it difficult to understand a basic fact of leverage. If I manage $1 billion, and I am often 10% more correct than others, my decisions can bring $100 million in value in a single judgment. With modern technology, massive labor, and capital, the multiplier of our decisions can be leveraged to increasingly higher levels. If I face a difficult choice, such as these questions: Should I marry this person? Should I take this job? Should I buy this house? Should I move to this city? Should I partner with this person in business? If you cannot decide, answer no. The reason is that modern society is full of choices. There are so many choices. We live on a planet with 7 billion people, and we can connect with everyone through the internet. There are hundreds of thousands of professions for you to choose from. There are so many choices. When you choose certain things, you are locked in for a very long time. Starting a business might take 10 years. Starting a relationship might take 5 years or more. Moving to a city might take 10 to 20 years. These are all decisions with very, very long-term impact. We only say “yes” when we are very certain. You can never be absolutely certain, but you must be very confident. If you have two choices, and they are relatively equal, then choose the path that is more difficult and more painful in the short term. The reality is that one path will endure short-term pain. The other path will feel pain further down the line in the future. However, your brain tries to avoid conflict and tries to avoid short-term pain. By definition, if two choices are similar, and one has short-term pain, then this choice is related to long-term gain. According to the law of compound interest, long-term gain is what you want. Your brain overvalues short-term happiness and tries to avoid short-term pain. Caffeine is another thing that trades long-term consequences for short-term benefits. Essentially, you must, through your life, replace bad habits you unconsciously acquire with good habits, committing to become a happier person.
13. On Happiness Confucius said that a person has two lives, and the second life begins when you realize that life is only one. So, when and how does your second life begin? (Confucius said: I never said that.) I read a quote by Blaise Pascal. It roughly means: “All of humanity’s unhappiness is because they cannot sit quietly in their rooms.” If you sit for 30 minutes and feel happy, you are successful. This is a very high state, but few people achieve it. The core skill you must learn is to be content with circumstances and go with the flow in most situations. You can get almost anything you want from life, as long as it is what you want the most. The first rule of handling conflict is: don’t be with people who frequently cause conflict. I am not interested in things that are not sustainable or difficult to sustain, including relationships full of problems.
14. The Top Priority of Life The top priority of my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my own health. First is my physical health. Second is my mental health. Third is my spiritual health. After that, is my family’s health. After that, is my family’s happiness. After that, I can do anything else in the world that I need to do. Basically, whenever you recommend a good habit to someone, they will find an excuse for themselves, and the most common excuse is usually, “I don’t have time.” When you hear this, you know they are saying, “This is not a high-priority matter.” If something is your top priority, you will do it. That is how life works. If you have 10 to 15 vague and non-urgent matters, you will ultimately not do any of them. What I do is decide that the top priority in my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my health. My physical health has become my top priority, so I can never say I don’t have time. In the morning, I exercise, no matter how long it takes, I insist on exercising. If I haven’t finished exercising, I won’t start the day’s work. I don’t care if the world is collapsing and melting; it can wait another 30 minutes until I finish exercising. Just like other things in life, if you are willing to make short-term sacrifices, you will have long-term benefits. “Easy choice, difficult life. Difficult choice, easy life.”
15. Don’t Fight Your Own Thoughts Don’t take yourself too seriously. You are just a monkey with a plan. Don’t make any decisions, don’t make any judgments; just accept everything. If I walk and do this for ten to fifteen minutes, I enter a very calm, grateful state. Non-judgmental consciousness is very useful to me. Another method I learned is to sit there, close my eyes, for at least an hour every day. You surrender to whatever happens—without effort. You don’t strive to do certain things, nor do you strive to oppose certain things. If thoughts flow through your mind, you flow with those thoughts. “If a thought comes, a thought comes. I don’t fight it. I don’t embrace it. I don’t think about it. I don’t reject it. I just sit there with my eyes closed for an hour, doing nothing.” This is a state of happiness, bliss, and tranquility. Once you have it, you don’t want to give it up. If you can gain an hour of happy freedom time just by sitting with your eyes closed every morning, that is priceless. It will change your life. All you have to do is sit there and do nothing. Just sit down. Close your eyes and say: “I just want to rest for an hour. This is an hour away from life, an hour where I do nothing.”
16. Let Consciousness and Mind Coexist Harmoniously Buddhists talk about consciousness and the self; they truly view your brain as a multi-layered mechanism: a core-level operating system is running, and then there are some applications running on top of it. I am returning to the operating system of my consciousness layer, which is always calm, always peaceful, usually happy and satisfied. I try to maintain this state instead of activating the “monkey mind” (referring to the mind below consciousness). The monkey mind is always worried, afraid, and anxious; it has incredible power, but I try not to activate it until I need it. If I run it non-stop for 24 hours, I will waste energy, and the monkey mind will become me; I am more important than my monkey mind. The mind itself is a muscle—it can be trained and regulated, but it has been haphazardly trained by society into a form that we cannot control. If you examine your mind with consciousness and intention, I think you can extract your own thoughts, emotions, ideas, and reactions, and then you can start reprogramming. You can rewrite this program according to your will.
17. How to Define Wisdom? A person understands the long-term consequences of what they do.
summary:
1. People Should Seek Wealth, Not Money or Status

People should not earn wealth through arduous work. Working 80 hours a week in a restaurant will not make you richer. Hard work is unavoidable, but it should be done in the right way. People should seek wealth, not money or status. If you believe wealth is unimportant, wealth will move away from you. Wealth is assets that continue to make money while you sleep. Without wealth-generating assets, when you sleep, you have no income; when you retire, you cannot keep earning money. In short, without wealth, you cannot achieve non-linear earning. Generally, wealth is created by starting your own company or by investing. Neither of these is achieved by putting in a massive amount of time; the ultra-rich, just like you, only have 24 hours every day.
title: Holy Book *Naval Compendium: Guide to Wealth and Happiness*

Modern economics covers many important concepts and theories. Here are some of the main concepts:
Supply and Demand Theory: Supply and Demand Theory is one of the most fundamental concepts in economics, describing the relationship between supply and demand in the market for goods and services. It involves the formation and regulation mechanism of prices.
Marginal Analysis: Marginal Analysis emphasizes the importance of considering marginal changes in decision-making. Marginal cost, marginal utility, marginal productivity, etc., are core concepts of marginal analysis.
Opportunity Cost: Opportunity cost refers to the highest value of the alternative or opportunity that is given up when a certain action is chosen. It emphasizes the impact of considering opportunity cost on economic behavior.
Utility Theory: Utility Theory focuses on individual preferences and utility. It studies how individuals maximize utility when faced with choices, involving concepts such as diminishing marginal utility and utility functions.
Production Function: The production function describes the relationship between inputs and outputs, i.e., how input factors are converted into output. The production function is an important tool for studying production efficiency and output growth.
Cost Theory: Cost Theory studies the cost structure and decision-making process in a firm’s production. It includes concepts such as fixed costs, variable costs, marginal costs, etc., which are highly significant for a firm’s operational decisions.
Market Structure: Market structure studies the number, size, and interaction methods of different market participants. Common market structures include monopoly, oligopoly, competitive markets, etc.
Information Economics: Information Economics studies the transmission and utilization of information in the economy. It considers the impact of information incompleteness and asymmetry on market efficiency and resource allocation.
Externality: Externality refers to the non-market impact generated by the actions of an economic agent on others or society. Externality can be positive (positive externality) or negative (negative externality).
Public Goods: Public goods are items that cannot be excluded from individual use, and one person’s use does not affect others. Public goods usually require government intervention for provision and maintenance.
